103098.text: A habitat with no birds counts as 0 birds for the \textbf{Ecologist} bonus card, so a player who has left any habitat empty scores 0 points for it.

104957.text: With \textbf{European Turtle Dove}, first draw 1 new bonus card, then choose exactly one of the three benefits: gain 1 [die] from the birdfeeder, lay 1 [egg] on any bird, or draw 1 [card].

108450.note: The answer also restates the general rule that drawn cards may come from the face-up tray or the deck unless the card specifies otherwise, which is rulebook text; the card-specific part is captured here. Ruddy Duck was named only as part of the scenario.
108450.text: \textbf{Red-Tailed Hawk} draws from the top of the deck, not from the 3 face-up cards on the bird tray, so its power can always be activated — there will always be cards in the deck.

108674.note: Official answer confirms a pink predator power counts as a predator succeeding when it gains food.
108674.text: \textbf{Sacred Kingfisher} is a predator. If it gains food with its power, that counts as a predator succeeding, which can trigger other players' powers that trigger when a predator succeeds.

109104.note: The 'once between turns' half overlaps the existing general ruling ``You may activate each `once between turns' power on a bird on your player mat once between each of your turns.'', but the nectar-source clarification is new.
109104.text: \textbf{Spangled Drongo} triggers when another player gains [nectar] for any reason, not only when gaining food from the birdfeeder. As a ``once between turns'' power, it can trigger only once between each of your turns.

109168.note: The answer states a broader principle (a wild does not satisfy a power looking for a specific icon), but it was given for Brown Falcon only.
109168.text: A [wild] food cost symbol does not count as an [invertebrate] or a [rodent] for \textbf{Brown Falcon}: a card whose food cost includes only [wild] is discarded rather than tucked.

110706.note: The underlying principle (all bonus cards must be scored) is general, but it was answered in the context of these two copying birds.
110706.text: You must score all of your bonus cards at the end of the game (even if you earn 0 [star] from them), so you cannot decline to score a bonus card because an opponent copied it with \textbf{Greater Adjutant} or \textbf{Indian Vulture} and would score more from it than you.

112570.note: Bonus cards do not receive general rulings via the pipeline, but this is card-scoped and names them directly.
112570.text: \textbf{Great Indian Bustard} can score bonus cards that specify ``at end of game'' or ``at game end,'' such as \textbf{Visionary Leader} and \textbf{Winter Feeder}, when its power is used mid-game.

116208.text: If \textbf{Spoon-Billed Sandpiper} is played at game end (for instance via a yellow power that lets you play a bird then), its power is still followed in full, including the portion allowing other players to discard any 2 resources to draw 2 new bonus cards and keep 1.

116933.note: The existing ruling on this card ("counts double toward precisely the end-of-round bonuses that count birds, not those that count other quantities") appears to conflict with Jamey's answer here that 2 eggs on the Woodpecker count as 4 eggs. A reviewer should reconcile the two.
116933.text: Only the quantity on \textbf{Eurasian Green Woodpecker} itself is doubled, not your whole total. For an [egg]-counting end-of-round goal, 2 [egg] on this bird count as 4 [egg]. For a goal that counts birds in a particular habitat or row, this bird counts only if it is there, and then counts as 2 birds instead of 1.

117963.text: \textbf{Common Myna}'s habitat restriction applies only to where it can be played, not to where it can move. If it copies a power that moves a bird to another habitat, such as \textbf{Blue Grosbeak}'s, \textbf{Common Myna} may move out of the [grassland].

119172.note: Bonus cards do not receive fanned-out general rulings, but a card-scoped ruling attaches directly.
119172.text: \textbf{Food Web Expert} counts only birds whose food cost is [invertebrate] and nothing else. A bird with any other food symbol in its cost, even as an alternative, counts for 0. The appendix reads: ``Count the number of birds that have [invertebrate] in their food cost and no other symbols.''

120367.note: Two separate answers in the thread (120369 for European Honey Buzzard, 120371 for Hawfinch) make the same point; combined into one ruling. The later exchange about a translation discrepancy is a localization issue, not a rules matter.
120367.text: When gaining food from the birdfeeder with \textbf{Hawfinch} or \textbf{European Honey Buzzard} after resetting it, dice showing the [invertebrate]/[seed] face count: \textbf{Hawfinch} may take the [seed] from such a die, and \textbf{European Honey Buzzard} gains the [invertebrate] from such a die along with all other [invertebrate] showing.

123416.note: The thread's first exchange (comment 123417) is thematic design chat about Common Myna and is not a ruling, so Common Myna is not attached.
123416.text: \textbf{Rose-Ringed Parakeet} copies only the ``When Played'' power itself, not the copied bird's food cost. Treat the power as if it were printed on \textbf{Rose-Ringed Parakeet}: copying \textbf{Eastern Imperial Eagle} or \textbf{Bonelli's Eagle} therefore does nothing, because \textbf{Rose-Ringed Parakeet} has no [rodent] in its own food cost.

125579.duplicates: This bird counts double toward precisely the end-of-round bonuses that count birds, not those that count other quantities. When in your hand this card does not count toward end-of-round bonuses. (Also the general ruling: "Only powers of birds played on a player mat can be used... does not count double toward the [card] in hand end-of-round goal.")

125661.note: The second question in the thread ("draw a bird card from the deck" vs. "draw a bird card") was also confirmed, but it is a general principle already reflected in this card's existing ruling about drawing from the deck and/or tray; recorded here only the card-specific part.
125661.text: When using this bird's power, the drawn cards are revealed: players look at them before choosing, rather than selecting blind.

126052.note: The answer is really a general rule about refilling the display at end of turn, but it was asked and answered in the context of Australian Ibis; a reviewer may want to promote it to a general ruling on turn-end display refill.
126052.text: The bird card display is refilled at the end of each player's turn, including the final turn of a round, so it is refilled after a turn using \textbf{Australian Ibis}. The round-end steps then completely refresh the card row.

126934.reject_reason: Digital-implementation bug report, redirected to app support; no rules clarification given.

127122.duplicates: If this bird already has the maximum number of [egg] on it, you may still use its power to tuck a [card].
127122.note: Already covered by the existing ruling on this card.
127122.text: If \textbf{Yellow-Headed Blackbird} already has the maximum number of [egg] on it, you may still use its power to tuck a [card]; you simply cannot lay an [egg].

127928.reject_reason: Misprint on box packaging; the printed card percentage is correct. Not a rules clarification.

127986.text: A [wild] food symbol does not count as [seed] for the \textbf{Bird Feeder} bonus card; only birds showing a [seed] symbol qualify.

128469.note: Official answer confirms nectar counts as a [wild] food for a discard cost and that discarded nectar goes to the spent pile. Reviewer may wish to generalise to other discard-a-[wild] powers, but this thread only names Crimson Chat.
128469.text: [nectar] may be discarded to pay the [wild] cost of \textbf{Crimson Chat}. The discarded [nectar] goes to the spent nectar area of your player mat.

128471.text: [nectar] may be cached with \textbf{House Crow}. Cached [nectar] is placed on the bird, not in the spent nectar area of your player mat.

129537.text: With \textbf{Galah}, you tuck 2 [card] from the deck behind this bird regardless of whether the chosen player gains a [seed].

133137.text: When the order of Game End powers matters, activate them in clockwise order starting with the player who has the first-player token.
133137.title: Game End power order

134235.note: Jamey's answer is a broad principle covering both examples asked (drawing bonus cards from \textbf{Philippine Eagle} and \textbf{Black-Tailed Godwit}). Note tension with the established ``you can take less of an action beneficial to yourself'' premise (ruling 20200404) — a reviewer may want to reconcile these. \textbf{North Island Brown Kiwi} added because thread 134886 settles the same point.
134235.text: If you choose to activate a power, you must follow through with it to completion. You cannot decline part of the power after seeing the cards you drew, such as refusing to keep a bonus card you drew.
134235.title: Activating a power

134886.note: Card text shown reads ``Discard a bonus card. If you do, draw 4 bonus cards, keep 2, and discard the other 2.'' while the question described drawing 2 and keeping 1 — a printing/version difference in the numbers, but the ruling is about the mandatory discard.
134886.text: If you choose to use \textbf{North Island Brown Kiwi}'s power, you must follow all of its instructions; you cannot skip discarding a bonus card and still draw bonus cards.

135135.reject_reason: Question concerns the artwork on the card (a chick on the bird's back), not a rules interaction; the answer that the bird counts for the beak-direction goal is already how the card's printed beak icon works.

135136.note: Two official comments: 135155 settles the Grey Shrikethrush case, 159953 clarifies that bird powers are not main actions. Combined into one ruling; provenance given as the later comment.
135136.text: \textbf{Loggerhead Shrike} triggers whenever another player gains any number of [rodent] during their ``gain food'' action, including [rodent] gained from a bird power activated during that action (e.g., \textbf{Grey Shrikethrush}). A bird power that gains food is not itself a main action; the main actions are the ones printed on the player mat, so gaining [rodent] via a bird power during the ``play a bird'', ``lay eggs'', or ``draw cards'' action does not trigger \textbf{Loggerhead Shrike}.

137154.note: Jamey phrased this as ``I would say'', but it plainly settles the question.
137154.text: You may not reset the birdfeeder before using \textbf{Western Screech-Owl}'s power, even if it contains only one food type, because you are not gaining food from the birdfeeder.

137366.note: Jamey's answer covers the general principle for copy powers, but is written here for the two cards named. Only the immediate scoring is addressed; the answer does not discuss whether the copied bird also scores that bonus card normally at game end.
137366.text: When \textbf{Rose-Ringed Parakeet} copies a neighbor's ``When Played'' power, resolve it as if the copied text replaced \textbf{Rose-Ringed Parakeet}'s own text: it applies to your board, not your neighbor's. Copying \textbf{Great Indian Bustard} therefore scores one of your own bonus cards, caching [seed] on \textbf{Rose-Ringed Parakeet}.

137367.text: \textbf{European Serin}'s power requires discarding all food tokens from your personal supply, not just all of one food type. You must have at least 1 food to activate it.

138246.reject_reason: Localization/translation errors; directed to the localization partner

138344.text: When using \textbf{Tufted Puffin}, roll the same set of dice all three times; dice that roll [fish] are not removed from the pool between rolls.

138372.note: Partially overlaps the existing \textbf{Anatomist} ruling about substrings that coincide with body-part names (e.g. \textit{wing} in \textbf{Burrowing Owl}), but adds the etymological/figurative case and the named cards. Jamey allows group consistency as an alternative.
138372.text: Words in bird names that only figuratively refer to a body part, such as the ``poll'' in \textbf{Blackpoll Warbler} or ``start'' in redstart names, do not count toward the \textbf{Anatomist} bonus card, since they are interpretations of a word rather than anatomical words. Groups may agree to count them as long as they are consistent.

138948.text: ``Resetting the birdfeeder'' means rerolling all the dice in the birdfeeder, however it comes about. \textbf{Laughing Gull}'s power can trigger (once between turns) whenever an opponent does this, including a reroll caused by all remaining dice showing the same face or only one die being left in the birdfeeder.

140638.text: \textbf{Laughing Gull}'s power triggers whenever the birdfeeder is reset during another player's turn, regardless of which effect caused the reset. For example, if another player's ``gain food'' action empties the birdfeeder because you took the last die with \textbf{Australian Owlet-Nightjar}, the birdfeeder reset on their turn still activates \textbf{Laughing Gull}.

142540.reject_reason: Request about future reprints/product plans, not a rules clarification.

142616.note: Existing ruling on this card says it counts double only for goals that count birds; this thread adds the specific case of the ``different point values on birds'' goal, where the answer is that it does not help. Applies to other ROUND END birds with the same power text, but only Cetti's Warbler was named.
142616.text: \textbf{Cetti's Warbler} does not help toward the \textbf{different point values on birds} end-of-round goal: counting the same bird twice still accounts for only one point value, and the goal looks for birds with different point values.

142740.reject_reason: Question about deck contents/availability, not a rules clarification.

142823.note: Answer was phrased as a general principle ("Unless the power specifies, you can choose any habitat"), but only Orange-Breasted Bunting was named, and this concerns the Americas hummingbird mechanic which wingsearch may not yet carry. Kept card-scoped; a reviewer may want to widen it to all attract/return hummingbird powers that do not name a habitat.
142823.text: When a power attracts or returns a hummingbird without specifying a habitat, such as \textbf{Orange-Breasted Bunting}, you may choose any habitat; it need not be the habitat where the bird with the power is played.

142892.reject_reason: Chat about whether a bird is in the expansion; no rules content.

143058.reject_reason: Question about expansion contents, not a rules clarification.

143103.note: Jamey states the original hummingbird cards work exactly as before and that the hummingbird column board is not designed to be placed at the end of the mat; neither is a durable card-level rules clarification worth attaching to a card page.
143103.reject_reason: Mostly expansion content speculation, component use outside its design, and campaign requests; the one rules-adjacent answer (original hummingbirds unchanged) is not a card ruling.

143116.reject_reason: Question about which birds are in the expansion, not a rules clarification.

143545.reject_reason: Replacement parts request, not a rules question.

143886.note: The thread also names the three Data Analyst and three Ranger bonus cards without giving their exact titles, so they are mentioned in the text but not listed in `cards`. Note that general rulings currently cannot reach bonus cards or hummingbird cards via the pipeline (see domain notes §4.8), so this is card-scoped on the bonus cards.
143886.text: Hummingbird cards are birds and count toward bonus cards in the ordinary way, including \textbf{Bird Bander}, \textbf{Ecologist}, \textbf{Ethologist}, \textbf{Passerine Specialist}, \textbf{Small Clutch Specialist}, and the Data Analyst and Ranger bonus cards.

144878.note: Yellow-Eyed Penguin is a fan-designed NZ promo card; the principle (playing a bird for free still grants when-played powers, but cost-referencing powers do nothing) may be worth a general ruling if a predicate for 'played for free' effects is written.
144878.text: A bird played for free with \textbf{Yellow-Eyed Penguin}'s power still triggers its ``when played'' power, but powers that refer to a paid cost have no effect. In particular, \textbf{Bonelli's Eagle} tucks no [card] when it is played for free.

145276.text: Food cached on this bird may only be spent on the cost of a bird power, not on the cost of playing a bird -- including a bird played via another bird's power, such as \textbf{Tufted Titmouse}.

145503.note: Thread also names Lineated Woodpecker, which was not supplied in the card list; the same ruling applies to it.
145503.text: \textbf{Great Kiskadee} and \textbf{Tropical Kingbird}: After moving with the action cube, continue activating birds only in the new habitat -- you do not activate the core action of the new habitat. For pink ``once between turns'' powers that trigger on another player taking a specific core action, the action taken is the one where the cube started, since the core action happens at the beginning of the turn.

146641.duplicates: Partially covered by existing rulings on both cards: \textbf{Long-Tailed Tit} -- "If a bird (e.g., \textbf{Common Buzzard}) is played on top of this one, the top bird is also placed horizontally and occupies both columns." and \textbf{Red Kite} -- "If this bird is played on top of a horizontal one (e.g., \textbf{Common Blackbird}), it is also placed horizontally and occupies both columns."
146641.note: This thread restates rules already present on both cards; the only new content is the explicit denial that the second space is freed. Reviewer may prefer to drop as duplicate.
146641.reject_reason: Red Kite played on Long-Tailed Tit: both cards already carry the answer.
146641.text: When \textbf{Red Kite} is played on top of \textbf{Long-Tailed Tit}, it is played directly on top of it and is also placed sideways, covering 2 [forest] spaces; the second space is not freed up.

146648.note: The general principle (only printed text counts for bonus scoring; copied powers are not remembered) could be broadened, but the answer addressed this specific pairing. Note wingsearch general rulings cannot reach bonus cards.
146648.text: \textbf{Rose-Ringed Parakeet} does not count toward the \textbf{Endangered Species Protector} bonus card even if it was used to copy a ``When Played'' power that scored or drew bonus cards. Only the abilities printed on the card matter during bonus scoring.

146899.note: Answer confirms attracting a hummingbird via Altamira Oriole triggers the hummingbird's benefit. Wingsearch stores hummingbird cards separately (hummingbirds.json), so this ruling only attaches to \textbf{Altamira Oriole}.
146899.text: When this bird's power attracts a hummingbird, you activate that hummingbird card's benefit.

147002.text: \textbf{Great Eared Nightjar}'s power looks for the [forest] icon printed on the drawn bird cards. Any bird with a [forest] icon counts, even if it also has other habitat icons.

147004.note: The official answer was phrased generally ("For card abilities, it's to/from any hummingbird slot") but only this card was named.
147004.text: When \textbf{Blue-and-Yellow Macaw} attracts a hummingbird, it may be placed in any hummingbird slot, not only one in the [forest]. Card abilities that attract or return hummingbirds are not limited to the habitat the bird is in.

147104.text: \textbf{Ivory Gull}: Food cached on this bird may be spent just like food in your personal supply whenever a bird power asks you to pay food to do something.

147159.text: An [egg] placed by this power can only be used to help pay the egg cost of the bird played on top of that egg; it cannot be spent on a bird played in another habitat or another slot. If the bird played on that slot needs no eggs (column 1), discard the egg.

147298.note: Jamey notes this holds "at least for now" -- confirmed with a Wingspan expert but flagged as possibly subject to revision. Also relates generally to Americas hummingbird spaces counting as spaces/slots.
147298.text: \textbf{Great Crested Grebe}: Empty hummingbird spaces in the row count as empty card slots for this power, so a lone bird in the first [wetland] slot with no hummingbird attracted draws 5 [card].

147452.note: The nectar half of the answer is specific to playing with Oceania nectar.
147452.text: This power only attracts hummingbirds; it does not let you return hummingbirds already on your player mat. You may attract only as many as you have open hummingbird spaces (1 or 2), and if all your hummingbird spaces are full you attract none. Nectar shown on an attracted hummingbird is gained as normal, even though this is a round end power.

147455.text: Standard tucking rules apply to the hummingbird tucked behind this bird.

147538.text: \textbf{Southern Lapwing}'s power is an independent choice ([egg] or [card]) for each empty slot in your [forest], so you may mix the two: with 5 empty slots you could lay 3 [egg] and draw 2 [card].

147924.note: Card's common name is printed "California Scrub-Jay"; thread writes "California Scrub Jay".
147924.text: \textbf{California Scrub-Jay}: ``Upgrading an action'' refers to the optional portion of the core action benefits printed on the player mat. Any time another player pays for and uses such an upgraded benefit -- including the choice between multiple upgrade options in a habitat, such as rerolling the birdfeeder or gaining an extra food -- it counts for this bird.

148731.text: When using \textbf{Titicaca Grebe}'s power, the drawn bonus cards are looked at, not chosen blindly: you look at them and choose 1, then the next player looks at the remaining cards and chooses 1, and so on.

149491.note: Jamey states "You'll just gain at most 1 food token from this power"; the choice of which food follows from that, since the power gains 1 of that food.
149491.text: If the card drawn with \textbf{Blue-Headed Parrot}'s power has both [seed] and [fruit] in its food cost, you still gain only 1 food token from the supply; choose which one.

149775.note: The question also named Great Kiskadee and Tropical Kingbird, which have the same power, but their card texts were not supplied so they are not listed.
149775.text: When \textbf{Lineated Woodpecker} moves with the action cube to another habitat and you continue your turn there, you only activate the brown powers in the habitat where your action cube currently is; you do not activate the remaining powers of the habitat it left.

150267.text: The eggs placed by \textbf{Rufous Hornero} are placeholders; they do not count as eggs in your preserve for any other purpose, so they do not count toward end-of-round goals or end-of-game scoring. Those spaces are still empty for purposes of bird powers that count empty spaces.

150554.note: Jamey first answered the opposite (comments 150562/150650), then corrected himself in 150843 after a player pointed out the repeat/copy distinction; only the correction should be recorded. The cards discussed (Gray Catbird, Northern Mockingbird, Great Kiskadee) were not included in the thread's card list, so `cards` is left empty for a reviewer to attach; \textbf{Barn Swallow} was mentioned only as an aside about the digital version and the ruling does not demonstrably bear on it.
150554.text: A ``repeat'' power (e.g., \textbf{Gray Catbird}) causes the other bird's power to trigger again on that bird itself; it is not a copy performed by the repeating bird. If the repeated power's condition is no longer met for that bird — for example, a migratory bird that must be the rightmost bird in its habitat is not at the right edge — the repeated power simply fizzles.

151248.note: Two official comments (151259 on ordering, 151361 on the Red Kite interaction); combined, cited to the later one.
151248.text: With \textbf{Garden Warbler}, the additional bird is played first and completely, including its own ``when played'' power, and only then is 1 [egg] laid on both birds. If the additional bird is \textbf{Red Kite} (or a similar bird) played on top of \textbf{Garden Warbler}, turning \textbf{Garden Warbler} into a tucked card, the egg laying still takes place.

155471.note: Thread also named Red-headed Woodpecker, but that card's text was not supplied, so it is omitted from the card list.
155471.text: These powers are literal and the ``may'' is a genuine choice: food you gain goes to your supply, and you may instead choose to cache any or all of it on this bird, where it scores 1 point at the end of the game instead of being available to spend.

156272.text: For powers that check which action types you used this round, such as \textbf{White Wagtail}, look at where each action cube ended up, as that is the game's way of remembering. A bird such as \textbf{Lineated Woodpecker} that moves with the action cube to another habitat therefore changes which action the cube records.

157464.note: Two separate answers combined; the hummingbird timing point is general (any brown ``end of turn'' power) but only \textbf{Wattled Jacana} was named in the thread. The follow-up question of whether you may refill an already-full tray was not answered. Consider splitting into two rulings.
157464.text: ``Refill'' the bird tray means placing a card from the deck on each empty slot of the bird tray; this is different from resetting the tray. Powers that say ``at the end of the turn'' trigger after hummingbird actions, since hummingbird actions happen during your turn.

157773.note: Jamey said he ``could see it going either way'' but leaned toward counting them; the answer is a lean rather than a firm ruling. Also note the pipeline currently cannot attach general rulings to bonus cards, but this is card-scoped to the bonus card itself.
157773.text: Hummingbird cards count toward the \textbf{Bird Bander} bonus card, as they can be placed in any habitat, even though they do not print multiple habitat icons.

158928.note: The same thread also settles two other points not attachable here: costs cannot be skipped (Western Capercaillie must give 1 bonus card away, though you may draw only 1 and give it away), and a birdfeeder reset caused by a player emptying it does trigger ``when another player resets the birdfeeder'' pink powers. Western Capercaillie was not in the supplied card list; a reviewer may wish to add those as separate rulings.
158928.text: \textbf{Canada Jay}: you may cache 1 [wild] from your personal supply and then immediately gain 1 food of that same type from the general supply in the same activation.

159034.note: The question was framed around the digital app; Jamey answered for the tabletop game. No specific card was named for this part of the thread, so `cards` is empty and this needs a predicate before it reaches any card page. The later part of the thread (bonus card keyword lists for fan packs) was not resolved.
159034.text: When a bird power has each player make a selection (such as each player gaining food from the birdfeeder or drawing a card), all players make their selections in turn order, then the active player continues activating the remaining brown powers in the current habitat until their turn ends.
159034.title: Resolving powers that involve all players

160965.note: Thread also mentions "blue black grasquit" (Blue-Black Grassquit), not listed among the cards provided; ruling written for Common Myna only.
160965.text: Copying a power places the other bird's power on \textbf{Common Myna} on your own player mat. If you copy a power that itself copies ``a power of a bird in the [grassland] of the player on your left'', you must still copy from another player's [grassland], not your own.

161439.reject_reason: Question about Wingspan Pocket's content and included birds, not a rules clarification.

161455.text: Hummingbird bonuses are only triggered when a hummingbird marker moves up the track, so moving a marker down with \textbf{Crested Oropendola} does not trigger the bonus of the space it lands on. To trigger a bonus again you must move down twice and then up at least once; an infinite loop is not possible.

161679.note: The Historian substitution in the German edition is a localization detail reported by a community member, not an official rules ruling.
161679.reject_reason: Localization and pricing/business question, not a rules clarification.

162024.text: \textbf{Loggerhead Shrike}'s power only triggers when another player gains [rodent] as part of the ``gain food'' core action of the [forest] habitat. It does not trigger from [rodent] gained or cached by bird powers.

162528.note: Question asked about ``star type as well as box nests''; Jamey confirmed. Consistent with the general rule that [star] nests count as any nest type.
162528.text: For \textbf{Orinoco Goose}, adjacent [star] nest birds count as [cavity] birds.

162588.note: Joe Aubrey said the power ``fizzles out'' because the cube is not currently on that bird; the follow-up question asking whether the bird nonetheless moves without the cube was not answered. Ruling written to state only that the power does nothing, which is the natural reading of ``fizzles out''.
162588.text: When \textbf{Great Kiskadee}'s power is repeated by another bird's power (e.g., \textbf{Gray Catbird} or \textbf{Northern Mockingbird}), the action cube is not on the \textbf{Great Kiskadee}, so its power has no effect.

162948.duplicates: Existing general ruling 'Powers': Only powers of birds played on a player mat can be used... does not count double toward the [card] in hand end-of-round goal. That covers point 1 in spirit but is about the end-of-round goal, not the Visionary Leader bonus card; point 2 is new.
162948.text: \textbf{Western Yellow Wagtail}'s power only functions once it has been played on your player mat, so it does not count double for \textbf{Visionary Leader} if it is still in your hand at the end of the game. For \textbf{Ecologist}, counting \textbf{Western Yellow Wagtail} twice does increase the number of birds counted in its habitat, so if all habitats otherwise hold an equal number of birds, that habitat is no longer the one with the fewest birds.

163039.reject_reason: Translation/replacement-card question for a non-English publisher; no rules content.

164589.reject_reason: Pocket-specific bonus/goal card scoring in a teach video; no full-game card ruling

164624.note: Answer is phrased as a principle covering any power that plays a bird; scoped here to the cards named in the thread. [Hand-edited: curly quotes normalised to TeX quotes.]
164624.text: When a bird is played using a ``game end'' (yellow) power such as \textbf{Dovekie} or \textbf{Yellow-Eyed Penguin}, you still gain the benefits of its ``when played'' (white) and ``game end'' (yellow) powers, even if the yellow power does not say so. \textbf{Gould's Finch} and \textbf{Grey-Headed Mannikin} state this explicitly only for extra clarity.

165076.note: Jamey also restated the general rule that you may reset the birdfeeder whenever you are gaining food (even mid-gain) if all dice show the same face, but for this card the reset is a single, one-time check.
165076.text: \textbf{Red-Legged Seriema}'s power looks at the birdfeeder after a single reset, checking simultaneously for [seed] and [rodent]. You may not claim some of those tokens and then reset the birdfeeder again to gain more.

167885.note: Bonus cards do not receive general rulings via the pipeline, but this is card-scoped so it attaches directly.
167885.text: Score 1 point for each [hummingbird] space on your hummingbird track that you have reached or exceeded.

168206.note: From the Pocket page: the questioner describes a Pocket version of \textbf{Red Junglefowl} whose text differs from the full-game card shown, so the ruling is not attached to that card. The underlying principle (the ``different birds'' limitation comes from the Lay Eggs action, not from bird powers) holds in the full game. Cards list left empty because no full-game card named in the thread matches the power described; a reviewer may wish to attach it to full-game birds that lay multiple eggs.
168206.text: The restriction that eggs must be laid on different birds applies only to the Lay Eggs action, not to bird powers. When a bird power lets you lay more than one [egg], you may lay them all on the same bird (subject to that bird's [egg] limit).
168206.title: Laying eggs with bird powers

168513.note: From a Wingspan Pocket thread. The bird named (\textbf{Common Blackbird}) has a completely different text in the full game, so no card is attached; the rule as stated holds generally in the full game for powers such as ``Gain 1 [seed] and 1 [invertebrate] from the birdfeeder, if available.'' A reviewer may want to build a predicate for multi-food birdfeeder powers.
168513.text: When a bird power tells you to gain more than one specific type of food from the birdfeeder, gain only the types that are actually present in the birdfeeder; the food that is not there is simply not gained, and the birdfeeder is not reset or refilled to find it.
168513.title: Gaining specific foods from the birdfeeder

168867.note: Corresponds to the established "'May' creates a choice" principle (comment 168922) already cited in the domain notes but not present as a ruling row in the examples shown.
168867.text: ``May'' creates a choice. On \textbf{Red-Headed Woodpecker}, you may decline to cache the [seed] and instead keep it as a normal food resource to spend later.
168867.title: May

169800.note: From a Wingspan Pocket thread, but the answer is stated as a general Wingspan principle and holds in the full game. The full-game \textbf{Galah} text shown (reset the birdfeeder / tuck 2 [card]) differs from the Pocket version described in the question, but it is still a power with two independent benefits, so the rule applies.
169800.text: When a bird power grants two independent benefits, you may resolve them in either order. If an arrow separates the two parts, resolve them left to right (cost, then benefit).
169800.title: Order of benefits in a power

30322.reject_reason: Trivia about the cover art, not a rules clarification.

30354.duplicates: When using this bird's power, if all [die] in the birdfeeder show the same face you may reroll before taking food. (and [general: Rerolling dice])
30354.reject_reason: No official answer to the reroll question in this thread; the rule is already covered by existing rulings on all four birds.

30879.duplicates: (Cartographer) ``The only keywords that qualify a bird to count toward this bonus card are those listed thereon, including \textit{prairie}...''; and the general ruling ``The word \textit{prairie} is a keyword for the \textbf{Cartographer} bonus card.''

31323.note: The official comment answers a general question about a 'repeat a brown power' bird and a 'move to another habitat' bird in the same habitat; Northern Mockingbird is the only such card named in the thread (via the later Q&A). Later in the thread Jamey revised the earlier 'copy' phrasing: the Mockingbird causes another bird to activate, which is already covered by an existing ruling on that card.
31323.text: \textbf{Northern Mockingbird} can only activate a bird that is currently in the same habitat. If a bird with a ``move this bird to another habitat'' power has already left the habitat, it can no longer be activated by \textbf{Northern Mockingbird}; conversely, if \textbf{Northern Mockingbird} activates that bird first, the activated bird may move to another habitat.

31792.duplicates: The only keywords that qualify a bird to count toward this bonus card are those listed thereon, those in the relevant sections of the expansion rulebooks...
31792.reject_reason: Already covered by the existing Photographer ruling listing which keywords qualify.

31884.note: Two questions, both answered by Jamey: comment 31916 (activation is not the Gain Food action) and comment 32122 (moving a bird via a power is not the Play a Bird action, so no egg cost). Only Loggerhead Shrike is named; the move-habitat half applies broadly to birds with 'move this bird to another habitat' powers.
31884.text: Activating a bird's power is not the same as taking the corresponding action. A bird activated by another power that gains [rodent] does not trigger \textbf{Loggerhead Shrike}, because the ``gain food'' action was not taken; likewise, a bird moved to another habitat by a bird power is not being played, so no [egg] cost is paid for the column it moves into.
31884.title: Activating a bird is not taking an action

32083.text: Powers are optional: the owner of \textbf{Osprey} may choose not to activate its power at all, in which case no player gains a [fish]. If the power is activated, another player may still decline to take their [fish].

32591.duplicates: The only keywords that qualify a bird to count toward this bonus card are those listed thereon, including \textit{prairie} (which is printed on this bonus card only in newer printings)
32591.reject_reason: Points to an errata list; the printing/typo content is already covered by the existing Cartographer ruling.

33055.text: Only birds printed with the [fish] icon count toward this bonus card; birds with the [wild] (any food type) icon do not count.

33197.note: Answer is a general timing restriction on the 2-for-1 food substitution rule; only Canada Goose was named.
33197.text: The option to pay 2 food of one type as a substitute for 1 food of another type applies only when playing a bird. It cannot be used to pay a food cost in a bird's power, such as discarding 1 [seed] for \textbf{Canada Goose}.
33197.title: Two food as one

33381.note: General rulings do not currently reach bonus cards in the pipeline (see §4.8), so the two bonus cards listed may not display it.
33381.text: A bird with a [star] nest counts as any nest type for every bonus card and end-of-round goal it can satisfy; the same bird may count toward multiple bonus cards at once, and toward goals in every round of the game.
33381.title: [star] nests

33575.text: \textbf{Bronzed Cowbird} has an egg limit of 0 and cannot hold eggs.

33594.duplicates: When using this bird's power to move this bird to another habitat, the action cube does not change habitats with it.
33594.reject_reason: Already covered by the existing ruling that the action cube does not change habitats with the bird.

34490.text: Caching the [seed] gained with \textbf{Blue Jay}'s power is optional. You may instead keep it as a food token to spend.

34968.note: Jamey answers both the specific and the general question: "Star nests are any/all nests all of the time throughout the game." Marked general because it spans every [star]-nest bird and every nest-referencing effect; cards list holds the pink egg-laying birds named in the thread.
34968.text: A bird with a [star] nest counts as any and all nest types at all times throughout the game, including for egg-laying powers, bonus cards, and end-of-round goals. A power such as \textbf{Yellow-Billed Cuckoo}'s that lays 1 [egg] on a bird with a [bowl] nest may lay it on a bird with a [star] nest.
34968.title: [star] nests

35190.note: Applies to all Oceania/European teal round-end powers; cards list holds only those named in the thread.
35190.text: Each player chooses the order in which they activate their own round end (teal) powers.
35190.title: Round end

35243.note: Goal-tile clarification; attached to the two example birds named in the thread.
35243.text: For the \textbf{food cost of played birds} end-of-round goal, the clarification to count only 1 food for birds with a choice in their food cost refers to the ``/'' in food costs. \textbf{Song Sparrow} ([invertebrate]/[seed]/[fruit]) counts as 1, while \textbf{Fish Crow} ([fish]+[wild]) counts as 2.

35443.note: The thread also answered that you may choose yourself as the starting player for ``each player gains 1 food from the birdfeeder, starting with the player of your choice'' powers; no such card was named, so it is not proposed here.
35443.text: \textbf{Loggerhead Shrike}'s power triggers only when another player takes the ``gain food'' action itself. It does not trigger when another player gains [rodent] from the birdfeeder through a bird power.

35622.reject_reason: Question about which set a bird appears in, not a rules clarification.

35681.duplicates: If a bird (e.g., \textbf{Common Buzzard}) is played on top of this one, the top bird is also placed horizontally and occupies both columns.
35681.note: Jamey's first answer (comment 35682) said you cannot play on top of the Roller and was explicitly retracted in comment 36218. Mostly covered by the existing European Roller / Common Buzzard rulings, but those do not state outright that playing on top of a sideways bird is permitted.
35681.reject_reason: The covering-bird-also-goes-sideways rule is already published on all four cards.
35681.text: \textbf{Common Buzzard} and \textbf{Red Kite} may be played on top of a bird placed sideways, such as \textbf{European Roller} or \textbf{Grey Heron}; the covering bird is then also placed sideways and occupies both spaces.

35725.note: Jamey's earlier comment 35726 first said "as if it's printed on the repeating bird" then edited to the opposite; Joe's 36250 is the settling answer and matches the existing Northern Mockingbird rulings. Existing rulings cover left/right and copy-power interaction but not the tucking/flocking/Citizen Scientist points.
35725.text: \textbf{Northern Mockingbird} does not take on the other bird's power; the other bird repeats its own power as if it were activated again. Cards tucked by a repeated tucking power (e.g., \textbf{Barn Swallow}) go behind that bird, not behind \textbf{Northern Mockingbird}, and food or [egg] costs are paid as that bird's power specifies (e.g., \textbf{Chihuahuan Raven} still requires discarding 1 [egg] from one of your other birds). A bird that gains tucked cards from another bird's power does not gain a flocking power, but does count for \textbf{Citizen Scientist}.

35746.duplicates: Existing Northern Bobwhite ruling: "This bird counts toward the \textbf{Photographer} bonus card." (and the Photographer ruling referencing Northern Bobwhite)
35746.text: The ``white'' in \textbf{Northern Bobwhite} counts as a color for the \textbf{Photographer} bonus card.

35763.duplicates: If this bird is played on top of a horizontal one (e.g., \textbf{Common Blackbird}), it is also placed horizontally and occupies both columns.
35763.note: Largely duplicates the existing Red Kite / Grey Heron horizontal-covering rulings; the only new content is that the covered bird is fully covered and its contents (feathers, egg capacity) no longer count. Birds to the right of the covered bird stay where they are (comment 36213).
35763.text: When \textbf{Red Kite} is played on top of \textbf{Grey Heron}, it is also placed sideways and completely covers \textbf{Grey Heron}, which becomes a tucked card. The covered bird's feathers, eggs and nest no longer matter.

35822.note: Official answer only confirmed what an action cube is; the counting phrasing follows the card text.
35822.text: The ``action cube'' referred to by \textbf{Dunnock} is the cube-shaped token a player places when taking a turn; count the cubes currently on the chosen player's [grassland] row.

35835.note: Answer was phrased as applying to "bonus cards like the Viticulturalist" (i.e. food-type bonus cards generally), but kept card-scoped to the card named.
35835.text: Birds that eat [wild] do not count toward the \textbf{Viticulturalist} bonus card; only birds showing the [fruit] icon qualify.

35848.duplicates: (Common Blackbird) "If a bird (e.g., \textbf{Common Buzzard}) is played on top of this one, the top bird is also placed horizontally and occupies both columns."
35848.note: Flagging a conflict: this 2019 answer says the bird played on top of a sideways bird keeps its normal orientation and goes on the right side, whereas the existing rulings on both cards say the top bird is also placed horizontally across both columns. The existing rulings presumably reflect a later, superseding official clarification — a reviewer should confirm which stands.
35848.reject_reason: Already covered by existing rulings on both cards, though the official answer here contradicts them

35952.text: \textbf{Loggerhead Shrike}'s power refers only to the core benefit of the ``gain food'' action, not to food gained from ``when activated'' bird powers. If a player gains [rodent] from a bird power such as \textbf{Eastern Screech-Owl}'s during their ``gain food'' action, \textbf{Loggerhead Shrike} is not triggered.

36014.duplicates: (Greylag Goose) "This bird counts double toward precisely the end-of-round bonuses that count birds... When in your hand this card does not count toward end-of-round bonuses."; also general ruling "Only powers of birds played on a player mat can be used."
36014.reject_reason: Part 1 duplicates the existing Greylag Goose ruling; parts 2 and 3 were deferred ("I'll check with the designer") and are already covered by existing rulings.

36200.note: The official answer restated the timing (move, then continue activating the originally chosen habitat) rather than directly saying "no resources from the new habitat"; the no-gain conclusion is inferred from that restatement and is consistent with the existing ruling that the action cube does not move with the bird.
36200.text: When this bird's power moves it to another habitat, you continue activating the originally chosen habitat; you do not gain the benefits of the new habitat.

36242.note: Comment 36245 corrects the earlier answer in 36243 (which said ties all count); comment 36727 adds the empty-habitat case.
36242.text: Score only one habitat for this bonus card, even if two or three habitats are tied for the fewest birds; the maximum score is therefore 10 points. A habitat with no birds counts as the habitat with the fewest birds, scoring 0 points.

36275.note: The official answer also states the general principle that ``your supply'' means your personal food and ``the supply'' means the general supply; kept card-scoped since only this card was asked about.
36275.text: The [seed] cached by \textbf{Eurasian Nutcracker} comes from your personal supply of food you have gathered, not from the general supply.

36280.note: The Mute Swan part of this thread (missing [flocking] icon) is already covered by an existing ruling on that card; the Greater Flamingo part is likewise already covered.
36280.text: The food types in these birds' powers are correct as printed; the specific food shown ([invertebrate] for \textbf{Common Swift}, [seed] for \textbf{House Sparrow}) applies, not ``any food''. The \textit{European Expansion} appendix uses examples to explain concepts and does not reproduce the exact text of every card.

36297.note: The question was about a single die in the birdfeeder; Jamey confirmed the reroll is allowed. Phrased to stay close to the standard reroll rule (all dice showing the same face / only one die left).
36297.text: When activating \textbf{Blue Jay}, if all dice in the birdfeeder show the same face you may reroll them all while looking for a [seed], per the normal rerolling rules; this includes when only 1 die remains in the birdfeeder.

36457.duplicates: Montagu's Harrier -- "Even when using this bird's power to play it on top of another bird, this bird may only be played in [grassland]."
36457.note: Essentially a duplicate of an existing Montagu's Harrier ruling; the only addition is the reasoning that the power is a WHEN PLAYED power.
36457.reject_reason: Montagu's Harrier already carries "Even when using this bird's power to play it on top of
36457.text: \textbf{Montagu's Harrier}'s power is a WHEN PLAYED power, so playing it on top of another bird still follows all the normal rules for playing birds, including habitat: it may only be played in [grassland].

36467.duplicates: Mute Swan -- "This bird's power is a [flocking] power; the [flocking] icon did not appear on the card in early printings..."
36467.reject_reason: Misprint/missing-icon report about future printings; the underlying icon ruling is already recorded for Mute Swan, and no rules question is resolved here.

36514.reject_reason: Request for updated component cards in a future expansion; no rules content.

36549.note: Comment 37711 refines 36551: the trigger resolves after all actions on the triggering card are finished. The Automa follow-up (41142) is out of scope for wingsearch.
36549.text: A pink power activates directly after the action that triggered it, once the triggering player has finished all the actions on the card that caused it. The player with the pink power completes it before the original player continues activating any further birds in their row.
36549.title: Once between turns

36587.note: Two official answers: comment 36588 (food returns to supply) and 45031 (spent nectar goes to the player mat). Cited the nectar one as it is the later, more specific ruling; reviewer may prefer 36588 for the first sentence.
36587.text: Food traded away with \textbf{Green Heron} goes back to the supply, not to the birdfeeder. If the food traded away is [nectar], it goes to the spent nectar space of your player mat instead.

36922.text: \textbf{Hooded Warbler} has no power, so nothing happens when an action cube passes over it while activating birds.

37275.note: The answer says "and others like it", i.e. other food-specific bonus cards (Fishery, Rodentologist, Bird Feeder etc.), but only Bird Feeder was named. Left card-scoped; a reviewer may wish to extend it to the other food bonus cards.
37275.text: Birds that eat [wild] do not count toward \textbf{Bird Feeder}; bonus cards that name a specific food icon only count birds showing that icon.

37277.note: The question asked about "optional" powers generally; the answer was given in terms of this card. Kept card-scoped, though it aligns with the general "'may' creates a choice" / "you can take less of an action beneficial to yourself" principles.
37277.text: \textbf{American Bittern}'s power is optional: if activating it would not benefit the player who activated it (for example, if that player does not have the fewest birds in their [wetland]), they may choose not to activate it at all.

37301.text: Eggs laid by any power are always taken from the general supply and then placed on a bird; they are never moved from another bird.
37301.title: Laying eggs

37396.note: Answer explicitly states it applies to every bonus card of that type, hence general scope; other food bonus cards (e.g. Rodentologist, Pisciform, Bird Feeder) are not named in the thread so are not listed in cards.
37396.text: A bonus card that refers to birds that eat a specific food counts only birds printed with that exact food icon; a [wild] icon does not count for it. This applies to every food-based bonus card, including \textbf{Viticulturalist}.
37396.title: Food bonus cards

37517.note: The designer's answer names turkeys and turkey vultures. The corresponding bird cards in the database are \textbf{Wild Turkey} and \textbf{Turkey Vulture}; reviewer may wish to restrict the ruling to the Cartographer page only if those bird pages should not carry it.
37517.text: ``Turkey'' does not count as a geography term for the \textbf{Cartographer} bonus card, and neither does ``turkey vulture'' (turkey vultures are named after the bird, not the country).

37614.duplicates: This bird counts double toward precisely the end-of-round bonuses that count birds, not those that count other quantities. When in your hand this card does not count toward end-of-round bonuses.
37614.note: Largely duplicates the existing ruling; the new detail is that a goal counting birds with a nest type and an egg still doubles the bird.
37614.text: This bird counts as two birds for an end-of-round goal that counts birds, including ``birds with [cavity] nests with at least 1 [egg]'' when it has at least one [egg] on it; eggs themselves are never doubled. It does not count toward the ``[card] in hand'' goal, since its power has no effect until it is played on a player mat.

37731.text: When using this bird's power, you may choose yourself as the player who gains food first.

37740.duplicates: This bird counts double toward precisely the end-of-round bonuses that count birds, not those that count other quantities.
37740.note: Already covered by the existing Cetti's Warbler ruling; only the worked example about sets of eggs is new.
37740.text: This bird counts double only toward end-of-round goals that count birds, such as ``birds in [wetland]''. It does not double eggs for the ``sets of [egg] in [forest][grassland][wetland]'' goal, nor any other goal that counts something other than birds (for example ``food cost of birds'').

37906.note: Answer is stated as a principle covering all pink powers that name a basic action; many such birds exist beyond the two named here (e.g. others triggering on "play a bird" or "draw cards" actions were not discussed, so the ruling is kept to the actions named).
37906.text: Powers that trigger when another player takes the ``lay eggs'' or ``gain food'' action refer only to those basic actions, not to laying eggs or gaining food from a card power. A card effect that lets a player lay an [egg] or gain food is not the ``lay eggs'' or ``gain food'' action.
37906.title: "Lay eggs" and "gain food" actions

37935.note: The answer is a general premise about tucking; scoped to card because only these two tucking birds were named. A reviewer may prefer to promote it to a general ruling titled ``Tucking''.
37935.text: There is no limit to the number of [card] that may be tucked behind a bird.

37945.reject_reason: Automa / solo mode; wingsearch does not cover solo play.

37949.duplicates: Greylag Goose: "This bird counts double toward precisely the end-of-round bonuses that count birds, not those that count other quantities." American Redstart: "This bird's power lets you take 1 food from the birdfeeder, as if [wild] were replaced by [die] in the power text."
37949.note: The same thread also confirms that \textbf{Greylag Goose} does not count double for the ``food cost of birds'' goal (already covered by that card's existing ruling: ``This bird counts double toward precisely the end-of-round bonuses that count birds...''), and that the [die] symbol and the birdfeeder ``color-wheel'' symbol mean the same thing (already covered by \textbf{American Redstart}'s existing ruling).
37949.reject_reason: Red-Bellied Woodpecker already carries "Because caching is optional, you may instead add
37949.text: \textbf{Red-Bellied Woodpecker}'s power is a single action with a choice: gain the [seed] from the birdfeeder, then decide whether to keep it in your personal supply or cache it on this bird.

37967.note: \textbf{Ethologist} is a bonus card; general rulings never reach bonus cards, but named rulings on bonus cards do display.
37967.text: At the end of the game, choose one habitat (row) of your birds and score 2 points per distinct power color present in that row, counting the four types of power color (including white/no power). The maximum score is 8 points, achieved when at least 4 birds in a single row each have a different power color.

38004.note: This simply restates the printed scoring on the bonus card; reviewer may consider it redundant.
38004.text: \textbf{Cartographer} awards a flat bonus, not points per qualifying bird: 3 points for 2--3 qualifying birds, 7 points for 4 or more.

38047.note: The official answer states only that pink powers cannot activate on their owner's turn and activate only during other players' turns; the second sentence of this ruling is an interpretation of the specific scenario asked (a tuck made by the pink power's owner during an opponent's turn). Reviewer may prefer to trim to the first sentence.
38047.text: A pink ``once between turns'' power can only be triggered during another player's turn, never during the owner's own turn. If a player tucks a [card] as part of their own pink power on another player's turn, that does not trigger their own pink power again, but it can trigger other players' pink powers such as \textbf{European Goldfinch} and \textbf{Snow Bunting}.

38093.note: Joe Aubrey's answer (comment 38101) was explicitly backed by designer Elizabeth Hargrave (comment 38113); the ''choose yourself'' half comes from comment 41378 in the same thread. Only Anna's Hummingbird was named, but Ruby-Throated Hummingbird has identical text.
38093.text: Any player may decline to take food from the birdfeeder when this bird's power is activated (they do not get a second chance during that activation), and the player activating the power may choose themselves to gain food first.

38158.text: \textbf{European Robin}'s power only applies at the moment it is activated: gain 1 food of a type you have already gained earlier in that same turn (for example, food gained by placing the action cube in the [forest] before moving the cube left onto this bird). It does not grant extra food at any other time.

38175.note: Thread also asked about 'once between turns' persisting after the last player's turn; that is already covered by the existing general rulings on pink powers, so it is not repeated here.
38175.text: \textbf{Sandhill Crane}'s power requires you to discard 1 [seed] in order to tuck 2 [card] from the deck; the discard is a cost, not something you may substitute or skip. \textbf{Blue Jay}'s ``You may cache it on this bird'' is a choice: either keep the gained [seed] in your personal supply or cache it on the bird, and the choice cannot be changed later.

38312.note: The \textbf{Bushtit} half of the thread is already covered by its existing ruling. The answer's broader premise (``generally in Wingspan you can elect to not do something beneficial to yourself'') is already in the corpus as ruling 20200404.
38312.text: You may activate this bird's power even if one or more birds in the column already have the maximum number of [egg] they can hold; lay [egg] on the birds that can receive them.

38362.note: The general half of this (refill the birdfeeder immediately when it empties, before activating powers) applies to all ``roll all dice not in birdfeeder'' powers, but the answer only worked through \textbf{Eastern Screech-Owl}.
38362.text: When the birdfeeder becomes empty, all dice are immediately refilled and rerolled before anything else happens, so this bird can roll at most 4 dice outside the birdfeeder.

38380.note: Thread also contains Jamey's answer that a brown power may be activated once per turn (comment 38381) and a Great Crested Grebe appendix quote (38461), plus an unanswered Red-Winged Blackbird question already covered by an existing ruling. Chose the Clark's Grebe answer as the durable new content.
38380.text: You do not need to reserve a [card] in hand to satisfy \textbf{Clark's Grebe}'s power; if you end your turn with no [card] in hand, there is nothing to discard and that is fine.

38484.note: The thread also contains an earlier exchange (comments 38485/38498) confirming that cached food only goes on played birds and that Eurasian Magpie can cache on birds without caching powers; the latter is already stated in the Appendix.
38484.text: For \textbf{Common Goldeneye}, birds with a [star] (wild) nest count as birds with a [cavity] nest.

38510.duplicates: The only keywords that qualify a bird to count toward this bonus card are those listed thereon...
38510.note: Arguably covered by the existing ruling that only listed keywords qualify, but this adds the specific, frequently-asked ``Turkey'' case (the designer researched the etymology and excluded it).
38510.reject_reason: Cartographer already carries the closed-list rule ("The only keywords that qualify a bird
38510.text: ``Turkey'' does not count as a geography term for the \textbf{Cartographer} bonus card; only the terms listed on the card qualify.

38516.note: The thread settles two things: teal powers recur each round (a general Oceania/European round-end timing rule), and "counts double" can exceed the printed 5-bird habitat limit when counting. Existing Eurasian Green Woodpecker ruling covers which goals count double applies to, not the recurrence or the 6th-bird point.
38516.text: A round end (teal) power activates at the end of every round after the bird is played, not only the round in which it was played; a bird played in round 1 can activate its round end power in all four rounds. A ``this bird counts double toward the end-of-round goal'' power can give you a virtual 6th bird in a habitat when counting birds for the goal.
38516.title: Round end powers

38839.note: Two official comments: 38841 defines "succeeds"; 41169 (Joe Aubrey, quoting the appendix) covers the tuck-to-pay case. The thread says "Goshawk"; in the full game the card is Northern Goshawk — reviewer should confirm the exact name before attaching.
38839.text: A [predator] ``succeeds'' when its action is successful, not when the bird is played — usually meaning it caches a food or tucks a card. If a bird such as \textbf{Northern Goshawk} uses its power to tuck cards instead of paying some or all of its food cost, that counts as both tucking a card and a [predator] succeeding, and triggers pink powers accordingly.

38927.duplicates: If you use this bird's power to play another bird with a ``play a second bird'' power, you may then use the latter bird's power to play yet another bird.
38927.reject_reason: Already covered by the existing ``play a second bird'' chaining ruling on all three cards.

38983.note: The thread writes "Loggerhead Strike"; the card is Loggerhead Shrike. Partly overlaps the existing Anatomist ruling that only listed keywords qualify, but adds the specific beak/head/horn determinations.
38983.text: Both ``beak'' and ``head'' are on the \textbf{Anatomist} list, so birds such as \textbf{Blue Grosbeak} and \textbf{Loggerhead Shrike} count. ``Horn'' is not on the list, so \textbf{Horned Lark} does not count; follow the printed list strictly, including the additions in the expansion rulebooks.

39066.note: The general principles (teal does not trigger pink; a pink power activates once regardless of the size of the trigger) could justify a general ruling, but the existing general ruling ``You may activate each `once between turns' power on a bird on your player mat once between each of your turns'' already partly covers the second point.
39066.text: \textbf{European Goldfinch}'s power activates only once between your turns, no matter how many [card] the other player tucked in the triggering event. Round end (teal) powers do not activate ``once between turns'' (pink) powers at all, since teal powers happen during no one's turn.

39094.reject_reason: Bird suggestion for a future expansion; no rules content.

39123.text: \textbf{Grey Heron} fills two [wetland] spaces and helps fill two columns, but it still counts as only a single bird (e.g., for the \textbf{birds in one row} end-of-round goal).

39534.duplicates: When using this bird's power, draw the [card] from the bird tray before it is refilled.
39534.reject_reason: Already covered by an existing Snow Bunting ruling
39534.text: When using \textbf{Snow Bunting}'s power, draw the [card] before the bird tray is refilled; refilling the tray is the last thing done at the end of a turn.

39576.note: Answer is phrased generally about [wild] but was given for Common Raven; kept card-scoped.
39576.text: When gaining 2 [wild] with \textbf{Common Raven}, the two food tokens may be of the same type or of two different types.

39793.note: Existing Rodentologist ruling clarifies ``eat [rodent]'' vs ``only eat [rodent]'' but does not address the [wild] symbol.
39793.text: \textbf{Rodentologist} counts only birds with the [rodent] symbol specifically; a [wild] food symbol (e.g., \textbf{American Crow}) does not count.

39961.reject_reason: Balance opinion / house-rule suggestion, no rules content

40298.reject_reason: Naming/localization discussion, not a rules clarification

40369.note: The answer is phrased around the Appendix entry for Eurasian Tree Sparrow and Joe notes ``following the normal pink power rules''; other pink birds with the same wording plausibly follow, but the answer only names this card, so the ruling is kept card-scoped.
40369.text: This bird's power can be activated and yield no food: if the birdfeeder contains no [seed], you gain nothing, and the power is still considered used, so it cannot be activated again until after your next turn. Whether the birdfeeder was reset first is irrelevant.

40424.duplicates: \textbf{Bushtit}: ``If this bird already has the maximum number of [egg] on it, you may still use its power to tuck a [card].''
40424.reject_reason: Already covered by an existing Bushtit ruling.

40663.note: European Magpie's card text was not shown in the thread listing, but the official answer explicitly names it as able to cache onto any bird.
40663.text: [seed] cached on \textbf{Eurasian Nuthatch} by another bird's power (e.g., \textbf{European Magpie}, which may cache onto any bird) can later be spent using this bird's power; the power applies to any [seed] cached on this card, not only [seed] cached by its own power.

40906.duplicates: The only keywords that qualify a bird to count toward this bonus card are those listed thereon... Substrings of bird names that coincide with names of body parts do not count toward the bonus when not referring to body parts (e.g., the \textit{wing} in \textbf{Burrowing Owl}).
40906.reject_reason: Already covered by an existing Anatomist ruling.

41156.note: Restates the rulebook's wild-food exchange rule; the thread is a general rules question, not about a specific card. Cards list holds only the birds named incidentally in the thread; reviewers may prefer to leave cards empty.
41156.text: When paying a bird's food cost, you may exchange any 2 food tokens to stand in for 1 food of any type you lack. This exchange may be used multiple times in the same payment (e.g., paying 4 [seed] to replace 2 missing foods). The 2-for-1 exchange is only available when playing a bird.
41156.title: Paying food costs

41417.text: The 2-for-1 food exchange may only be used when paying the food cost to play a bird. It cannot be used to satisfy a food requirement anywhere else, such as discarding [seed] for \textbf{House Sparrow}'s power.
41417.title: 2-for-1 food exchange

41507.reject_reason: Speculation about a future habitat; designer commentary on bird list design, not a rules clarification.

41618.note: Answered during the Oceania preview, before the Oceania rulebook was released; the rulebook states the same. Nectar is not accepted where a power names a specific food.
41618.text: [nectar] is wild for playing birds and may be spent for any food in a bird's cost, including a single [nectar] to pay a cost of 1 [seed]. [nectar] cannot be substituted when a bird's power refers to a specific food type.
41618.title: Nectar

41718.reject_reason: Design/flavor question about the wingspan asterisk; not resolved as a rule

41723.reject_reason: Question not resolved; answer defers to a future post

41724.text: Using a yellow (game end) power is optional; you may choose not to activate it.
41724.title: Yellow powers

41749.reject_reason: About the range map artwork, not a rules question

41776.text: The \textbf{Great Horned Owl}'s beak points straight forward, neither left nor right. The rulebook includes a list of birds whose beaks point neither left nor right, and the \textbf{Great Horned Owl} is on it.

41797.note: Relevant to the Oceania end-of-round goal about beak direction.
41797.text: The \textbf{Wrybill}'s beak points to the left, even though the bird faces forward. The rulebook lists the birds that face forward but whose beaks point left or right.

41823.note: Definition is printed in the Oceania rulebook; it applies to every bird power referring to adjacent birds, hence general scope.
41823.text: Adjacent birds are those immediately to the left, right, above, or below the bird in question.
41823.title: Adjacency

41877.reject_reason: Question about expansion contents; no rules content.

41896.note: The thread's main official clarifications concern the two Oceania cockatoos (each cockatoo card names the specific food all players gain; Joe Aubrey corrected Jamey on this), but those cards are not in the supplied card list, so no ruling is attached to them. The balance discussion about Wedge-Tailed Eagle and Butcherbird is opinion, not a rule; the over-65cm point restates printed card text and could be rejected as redundant.
41896.text: \textbf{Wedge-Tailed Eagle} looks for birds with a wingspan \textit{over} 65cm, unlike most predators, which look for wingspans under a given size.

41898.reject_reason: Speculation about bird selection and future promo packs; no rules content.

41910.duplicates: Partially covered by the existing Eurasian Nuthatch ruling ``You may spend a [seed] cached on this bird anytime you can spend a [seed] from your supply.'' but this adds the explicit discard-cost/Sandhill Crane case.
41910.text: A [seed] cached on \textbf{Eurasian Nuthatch} may be spent to pay the discard cost of another bird's power, such as \textbf{Sandhill Crane}'s ``Discard 1 [seed] to tuck 2 [card] from the deck behind this bird.''

41917.note: Jamey answered only the play-a-bird case. The community follow-up that [nectar] cannot substitute in food-specific bird powers was not confirmed by an [OFFICIAL] reply, so it is not included here.
41917.text: [nectar] may be substituted for any of the 5 other food types when paying the food cost to play a bird. For example, \textbf{Hooded Warbler} costs [invertebrate][invertebrate], so it can be played by paying [invertebrate][invertebrate], [invertebrate][nectar], or [nectar][nectar].
41917.title: Nectar is wild

41947.note: Two officials answered: Jamey (41948) said teal powers are optional; Joe (42821) added the partial-benefit point. Source set to the later comment, which covers the fuller answer. The optional-teal-power part may warrant a separate general ruling.
41947.text: Round end (teal) powers are optional. With \textbf{Black Redstart} you may also take less of the benefit---for example, laying [egg] on only some of the birds in the chosen habitat rather than all of them.

41953.text: The [wild] discarded for \textbf{Common Starling} may be a mix of any food types. Discarding food is a way of spending it, so [nectar] discarded for this power is placed on the appropriate spent nectar space of your player mat.

42071.text: \textbf{Common Cuckoo} correctly has no nest type and no egg limit; as a brood parasite it lays its eggs in other birds' nests, matching its power.

42084.note: The thread does not name the bonus card explicitly; the bonus card requiring a body part in the name is \textbf{Anatomist}. Jamey adds that some players houserule otherwise.
42084.text: \textbf{Bushtit} does not officially count for the \textbf{Anatomist} bonus card (birds with a body part in their name).

42087.reject_reason: Automa / solo mode question; wingsearch does not cover solo play.

42174.reject_reason: Speculative/trivia about a color word with no matching bird; no rules question resolved.

42297.duplicates: The only keywords that qualify a bird to count toward this bonus card are those listed thereon...
42297.reject_reason: Answer sidesteps whether "meadow" qualifies, calling it moot; no durable clarification. Existing Cartographer ruling already lists qualifying keywords.

42349.note: Thread also contains: Pileated Woodpecker two eggs must go on different birds (already an existing ruling, comment 42354), players may look through discard piles, and round-end/end-game phases do not activate pink powers (partly covered by existing 'Once between turns' general rulings). Only one proposal per thread allowed, so the Kingfisher/Vulture answer from comment 43416 is proposed here; a reviewer may want to add the discard-pile and round-end answers separately.
42349.text: Gaining food from the birdfeeder with the \textbf{Sacred Kingfisher}'s power counts as a successful [predator] action, so it can trigger another player's power that responds to a successful predator (e.g., the \textbf{Turkey Vulture}). It cannot trigger the pink power of the player whose turn it is, because the \textbf{Sacred Kingfisher}'s power resolves as the final step of that player's turn, not between turns.

42385.note: Thread combined two answerable points (goal composition, and Common Blackbird counting as one bird) plus one Automa question, which was omitted. The goal tile itself is not in the cards list, so the ruling is attached to the birds named.
42385.text: The \textbf{white \& no powers} end-of-round goal counts both birds with ``when played'' powers (white cards, e.g. \textbf{Common Blackbird}) and birds with no powers at all (e.g. \textbf{American Woodcock}, \textbf{Wild Turkey}). \textbf{Common Blackbird}, though placed sideways across 2 [forest] spaces, still counts as only 1 bird for goals and bonus cards that count birds.

42391.text: Any bird with 4 or more [egg] on it at game end counts toward this bonus card; the number does not have to be exactly 4.

42483.duplicates: The only keywords that qualify a bird to count toward this bonus card are those listed thereon and those in the relevant sections of the expansion rulebooks.
42483.note: Officially only the listed words count, so \textbf{Ruff} does not qualify for \textbf{Anatomist} unless a rulebook adds the word; this is exactly the existing ruling's content.
42483.reject_reason: Already covered by existing Anatomist ruling; rest is future-expansion speculation

42504.reject_reason: Chat/speculation about which birds appear in an expansion

42571.note: The existing Anatomist ruling covers the general principle but does not name \textit{back} or \textbf{Canvasback}; this adds the specific case and puts it on the Canvasback card page.
42571.text: \textit{Back} is a body part for this bonus card, as listed in the \textit{European Expansion} rulebook (``Anatomist (birds with body parts in their names): back, leg, toe''), so \textbf{Canvasback} counts toward it.

42580.duplicates: The only keywords that qualify a bird to count toward this bonus card are those listed thereon, those in the relevant sections of the expansion rulebooks ... Substrings of bird names that coincide with color names do not count toward this bonus when not referring to colors
42580.note: Answer restates that only the listed words (plus expansion rulebook additions) count; 'pine' is not a color word.
42580.reject_reason: Already covered by existing Photographer ruling on qualifying keywords

42661.reject_reason: House-rule/balance discussion; no rules clarification given.

42698.text: You tuck 2 [card] behind \textbf{Galah} regardless of whether the chosen player is able to gain a [seed] from the birdfeeder.

42743.duplicates: This bird counts double toward precisely the end-of-round bonuses that count birds, not those that count other quantities.

The existing ruling on both cards already covers the underlying principle, so this is largely a duplicate; the filled-columns example could be added as a clarification if desired.
42743.text: This bird does not count double toward end-of-round goals that count something other than birds, such as \textbf{filled columns}: it counts only in the column it occupies.

42788.reject_reason: Requests/speculation about future expansion bird choices; no rules content.

42814.note: Answer confirms Laughing Kookaburra counts as a predator power for other players' ``when another player's [predator] succeeds'' powers.
42814.text: \textbf{Laughing Kookaburra} has a [predator] power. If another player activates it and it succeeds (they gain a food), \textbf{Black-Billed Magpie}'s power triggers and you gain 1 [die] from the birdfeeder.

42859.note: Answer is a general clarification of the [wild] icon; the two ravens are the cards the rulebook passage names, so they are listed for immediate fan-out.
42859.text: The [wild] (``any food'') symbol includes [nectar] among the foods you may choose. You are never obligated to choose [nectar]; it is simply one of the options for paying an ``any food'' cost or gaining an ``any food'' resource.
42859.title: [wild] and nectar

42871.note: Grey Shrikethrush is the only card in this thread whose text was shown; the ruling is about nectar payment generally, which spans all birds with food costs.
42871.text: [nectar] is wild for the purpose of paying bird costs, so it may be spent in place of any specific food type. A [nectar] icon in a bird's cost, however, must be paid with [nectar] and cannot be paid with another food; only a [wild] icon accepts any food (including [nectar]).
42871.title: Nectar as a wild food

42877.duplicates: If you use this bird's power to copy the power of a bird that lets it move to another habitat---and this bird satisfies applicable conditions (e.g., being the rightmost bird in its habitat)---this bird may move to that habitat, even one in which it cannot be played.
42877.note: The Lyrebird/Tūī half is already covered by an existing ruling on both cards; the only possibly new content is the general statement that habitat eligibility matters only at play time, which would also apply to Chimney Swift.
42877.text: Habitat restrictions matter only when a bird is played. Afterwards, powers such as \textbf{Chimney Swift}'s---including when copied by \textbf{Superb Lyrebird} or \textbf{Tūī}---may move a bird into a habitat where it could not originally have been played.

42899.note: Jamey answered without the cards in front of him, but the condition he attached ("if the ability looks for other players to gain nectar while taking the 'gain food' action") does not apply: Spangled Drongo's power is unconditional.
42899.text: Receiving [nectar] as a gift counts as gaining [nectar], so when a player uses \textbf{Red-Winged Parrot} to give a [nectar] to another player, the receiving player has gained [nectar] and \textbf{Spangled Drongo} may be activated by it.

42906.reject_reason: Component availability question; the Anatomist keyword remark was not answered

43067.text: With \textbf{Kea}, you first draw 1 bonus card, then decide how many additional bonus cards you want to draw and discard the corresponding amount of food. This is a one-time decision. Among all the bonus cards drawn using this bird's power, you keep only 1.

43078.duplicates: The only keywords that qualify a bird to count toward this bonus card are those listed thereon, those in the relevant sections of the expansion rulebooks... Substrings of bird names that coincide with color names do not count toward this bonus when not referring to colors
