43078.text: Only the color words listed on the \textbf{Photographer} bonus card (or listed in expansion rulebooks) count. ``Tan'', as in \textbf{Western Tanager}, is not one of them.

43213.text: Only one scoring category on a bonus card is scored. With this bonus card you score either for 1 set of the 4 nest types or for 2 or more sets, not both.

43218.text: The two statements in \textbf{Galah}'s power are not connected. The chosen player resets the birdfeeder and gains a [seed] only if one is available, but you tuck 2 [card] from the deck behind this bird regardless of whether they gained a [seed].

43230.reject_reason: Question about which birds are in an expansion, not a rules clarification.

43291.text: Adjacent birds with the exact same wingspan count as part of an ascending or descending sequence for this bonus card.

43309.text: The ``normal cost'' paid for the additional bird played with this power includes any [egg] required by the column it is placed in, even if you already paid [egg] to play a bird this turn.

43329.note: Same underlying principle as thread 43213 (only one category of a bonus card scores). Cartographer is the card actually asked about; Mechanical Engineer included because the companion thread resolves the same rule for it.
43329.text: A bonus card with tiered scoring awards only the amount for the tier reached, not points per qualifying bird. On \textbf{Cartographer} you must have at least 2 qualifying birds to score 3 points and at least 4 to score 7 points.
43329.title: Bonus card scoring tiers

43472.text: \textbf{Brown-Headed Cowbird} has no nest type, so it does not count toward the \textbf{Site Selection Expert} bonus card; it is not treated as a [star] nest.

43556.note: The official answer is phrased for ``bonus cards like the Rodentologist'', i.e. food-type bonus cards generally, but only Rodentologist was named. Reviewer may wish to extend to other food-icon bonus cards (e.g. \textbf{Fishery}, \textbf{Bird Feeder}, \textbf{Omnivore Expert}).
43556.text: Only birds with a [rodent] icon in their printed food cost count toward the \textbf{Rodentologist} bonus card; a [wild] icon does not count.

43572.note: The earlier part of the thread (Black-Shouldered Kite) concerns Automa play only and is out of scope for wingsearch.
43572.text: With \textbf{Kea}, you keep only 1 bonus card out of all the bonus cards you drew with this power, including the first one drawn before discarding [wild].

43586.reject_reason: Balance opinion; official answer only confirms there is no misprint.

43607.text: The tucking part of \textbf{Galah}'s power is not conditional on the first part: you tuck 2 [card] from the deck behind this bird regardless of whether the other player gains a [seed] from the reset birdfeeder.

43665.duplicates: Existing rulings already cover this: \textbf{Coal Tit}: ``When a bird with a `copy' power (e.g., the \textbf{Superb Lyrebird}) copies this bird's power, that bird retains the ability to spend [seed] cached on it until the end of the turn but no longer.'' and \textbf{Superb Lyrebird}/\textbf{Tūī}: ``...if it copies the \textbf{Coal Tit}'s power, it retains the ability to spend [seed] cached on this bird until the end of the turn but no longer...''

43665.reject_reason: Duplicate of rulings already on all three cards -- and where it differs, it is the weaker
43665.text: When \textbf{Tūī} or \textbf{Superb Lyrebird} copies the \textbf{Coal Tit}'s power, it caches a [seed] and may spend [seed] cached on it while that power is being activated. Once the activation is finished it keeps any cached food but loses the ability to spend it, until the power is copied again on a later turn.

43673.note: Jamey answered without the card in front of him, but the answer is a plain statement of the general cached-food rule and applies to Korimako's discard cost.
43673.text: The [rodent] discarded for \textbf{Korimako}'s power must come from your food supply. Cached food may only be spent when a card specifically refers to cached food; otherwise it is only worth points.

43799.text: This bird's power allows resetting or refilling the tray only once; you may not keep resetting until a [cavity] or [star] nest bird appears.

43809.duplicates: This bird counts double toward precisely the end-of-round bonuses that count birds, not those that count other quantities.
43809.note: Largely covered by the existing Greylag Goose ruling; this thread adds the worked examples (``birds in one row'', ``ground nest birds with eggs'' count double; ``eggs in wetland'' does not). Reviewer may prefer to merge the examples into the existing ruling rather than add a new row.
43809.text: \textbf{Greylag Goose} counts double toward any end-of-round goal that counts birds, such as ``birds in one row'' or ``[ground] nest birds with [egg]''. It does not count double toward goals that count something other than birds, such as ``[egg] in [wetland]''.

43820.text: \textbf{Forster's Tern} requires discarding from your hand, so if your hand is empty at the end of your turn (for instance because you tucked all your cards with \textbf{Common Chiffchaff}), you discard nothing.

43909.text: [nectar] counts as a food type for this bird's power, so you may choose [nectar] and all players gain 1 [nectar] from the supply.

43914.duplicates: When a bird with a ``copy'' power (e.g., the \textbf{Superb Lyrebird}) copies this bird's power, that bird retains the ability to spend [seed] cached on it until the end of the turn but no longer. / When this bird copies another bird's power, it retains any effects specified in the copied bird's power text as long as those effects may occur but not beyond the end of the turn.
43914.reject_reason: Already covered by existing rulings on Superb Lyrebird, Tūī and Eurasian Nuthatch
43914.text: When this bird copies the power of a bird that lets it spend food cached on it, it may spend that cached food only until the end of the turn in which it copied the power.

43956.text: This bird's power looks for a specific icon in the drawn card's food cost, so a [wild] food cost does not count as an [invertebrate] or a [rodent].

43972.note: Jamey's answer addresses only the counting of separate icons; the later community comment about food1/food2/food3 (``or'' costs, e.g. \textbf{Orange-Footed Scrubfowl}) was not confirmed by an official reply, so it is not included here. Named cards are the examples raised in the question; the goal tiles themselves are not cards in the database, so scope is general. [Hand-edited: the model wrote an invalid [food] marker; reworded, meaning unchanged.]
43972.text: For end-of-round goals that name two food types in the food cost of your birds, count every icon of either type printed in the food costs of your played birds; a single bird does not need to require both. For example, with 5 [fruit] icons and 8 [seed] icons among your played birds, your number for the goal is 13.
43972.title: [food]+[food] in food cost goals

44644.duplicates: When using this bird's power to discard another bird from your mat, all food cached on that bird, [egg] laid on that bird, and [card] tucked under that bird are discarded.
44644.reject_reason: Already covered by the existing Southern Cassowary ruling; the rest of the thread is about rulebook wording/errata.

44739.text: \textbf{Galah}'s two statements are independent of each other. You always tuck 2 [card] behind this bird, regardless of whether the chosen player gains a [seed] when resetting the birdfeeder.

44861.note: The official answer only states the first sentence (pink powers activate only on other players' turns); the consequence for the specific chain asked about is inferred from it. Existing "Once between turns" general rulings cover related timing but not this restriction.
44861.text: Your own pink powers can only be activated during other players' turns, never during your own turn. A player tucking a [card] on their own turn does not activate their own \textbf{Snow Bunting} or \textbf{European Goldfinch}, and one player's pink power triggering does not trigger their opponent's identical pink power on that same turn.
44861.title: Once between turns

44908.duplicates: If this bird is played on top of a horizontal one (e.g., \textbf{Common Blackbird}), it is also placed horizontally and occupies both columns. / If a bird (e.g., \textbf{Common Buzzard}) is played on top of this one, the top bird is also placed horizontally and occupies both columns.
44908.reject_reason: Already covered by existing rulings on both cards.

45000.text: When counting birds in your [grassland] for this bird's power, include \textbf{Plains-Wanderer} itself. If it were excluded, the power would say ``each other bird''.

45006.note: Complements the existing ruling that ``trading'' counts as ``spending''; this thread specifies where the nectar physically goes.
45006.text: Trading a [nectar] token with this bird's power counts as spending it, so the traded [nectar] goes to your player mat rather than back to the supply.

45306.text: \textbf{Black-Billed Magpie} is not a predator bird and does not count for the \textbf{Falconer} bonus card; a bird is a predator only if it has the [predator] icon before its power text.

45314.text: You cannot use the power of \textbf{Gould's Finch} or \textbf{Grey-Headed Mannikin} if you have no open space in the habitat for the bird: if you can't play the bird, you don't get to use its ``when played'' or ``game end'' power either.

45420.note: Oceania rulebook page 11 lists birds whose beaks point in neither direction.
45420.text: \textbf{Eastern Screech-Owl}'s beak does not point in either direction, so it counts for neither the \textbf{beaks pointing left} nor the \textbf{beaks pointing right} end-of-round goal. (This is listed on page 11 of the Oceania rules.)

45467.note: Official answer quotes the rulebook appendix. The French appendix wording (``au moins 4 œufs sur eux'') was flagged as unclear but no correction was promised.
45467.text: Count only bird cards that have at least 4 [egg] tokens sitting on them at game end; eggs printed on the bird card do not count.

45516.note: Existing \textbf{Photographer} ruling lists qualifying keywords but does not mention \textit{rainbow} explicitly; this adds the specific exclusion (relevant to birds such as \textbf{Rainbow Bee-eater} and \textbf{Rainbow Lorikeet}).
45516.text: \textit{Rainbow} is not a color and does not count toward this bonus card.

45552.note: Thread also contains an unresolved art-direction question about \textbf{Eurasian Magpie} (Jamey did not have the card in front of him), so that card is not attached. The ruling concerns the player mat rather than any card, so no cards can be listed; a reviewer will need a predicate or another home for it.

45552.text: The bonus at the end of a full row of action spaces on the player mat may be used only once per turn: exactly 1 [card] discarded for 1 food, or 1 food spent for 1 [egg].
45552.title: Full-row bonus

45808.note: Jamey confirmed the specific 2-player Lyrebird-copies-Tūī play as legitimate; wording generalised slightly to cover the mirror case since both cards carry the same copy power.
45808.text: \textbf{Superb Lyrebird} and \textbf{Tūī} may copy each other's copying power. Doing so lets you copy a brown power in the relevant player's [forest], which in a 2-player game can mean copying one of your own brown powers.

46794.text: The player you choose to give the [rodent] to when using \textbf{Black-Shouldered Kite}'s power must accept it; they cannot decline in order to prevent you from laying eggs.

46807.duplicates: The only keywords that qualify a bird to count toward this bonus card are those listed thereon...; On this bonus card ``name'' refers only to the common name, not the scientific name.
46807.note: The keyword-list and scientific-name points duplicate existing rulings on all three bonus cards; the genuinely new parts are that a bird may count for multiple bonus cards and that predator dice rolled outside the birdfeeder (e.g. \textbf{Anhinga}) are rolled outside the tray. The egg-sets and once-between-turns answers also duplicate existing general rulings. A reviewer may prefer to split or drop this.
46807.text: The only words that count for \textbf{Anatomist}, \textbf{Cartographer}, and \textbf{Photographer} are those listed on the bonus cards themselves or in the expansion rulebooks; no other words count, and the scientific (Latin) names of birds are never considered. A single bird may count for more than one bonus card. Other language editions handle these bonus cards differently, so consult the rulebook of the edition being played.

46868.reject_reason: Suggestion about future card design; no rules content resolved.

47476.text: The condition ``If its wingspan is over 65cm'' is correct and not a misprint; unlike other predators, this bird tucks the drawn [card] when the wingspan is large.

47787.text: End-of-round goals are scored before end-of-game powers are activated (steps 4 and 6 of the ``End of Round Reference'' tile included with the \textit{Oceania Expansion}). Score the end-of-round goal first, then activate \textbf{Australian Magpie}, so discarding [egg] with its power cannot change your score for an egg-based goal.

47813.duplicates: This bird counts double toward precisely the end-of-round bonuses that count birds, not those that count other quantities. When in your hand this card does not count toward end-of-round bonuses.
47813.reject_reason: Already covered by the existing \textbf{Eurasian Green Woodpecker} ruling and the general "Powers" ruling.

47864.note: Thread bundles four separate answers. The dice/birdfeeder part is card-relevant to predator-style powers (Anhinga is the example named); the Brown Pelican part is card-specific; the ``player(s) with the fewest'' and egg-holding parts are general. A reviewer may wish to split this into separate rulings: (a) Brown Pelican / when-played cost timing, (b) roll all dice not in birdfeeder, (c) ties on ``player(s) with the fewest'', (d) eggs cannot be held off-mat.
47864.text: Powers that say ``Roll all dice not in birdfeeder'' are always resolved outside of the birdfeeder: do not roll those dice back into the birdfeeder. Only the dice rolled outside the birdfeeder are considered, not the dice sitting in the birdfeeder. If there are no dice outside the birdfeeder, this power has no dice to roll and gains nothing. Also, a ``When Played'' power resolves only after the bird has been played, so its cost must be paid first---you cannot use \textbf{Brown Pelican}'s power to gain the [fish] needed to pay for it. When a power refers to the ``player(s) with the fewest'' something, the ``(s)'' means that if several players are tied for the fewest, they all gain the benefit. Eggs must always be placed on a nest with available space; you may not hold eggs to the side of your player mat.
47864.title: Roll all dice not in the birdfeeder

47900.note: Answer was phrased as applying to any power worded ``Gain ... You may cache it on this bird'', but only \textbf{Clark's Nutcracker} was named.
47900.text: When activating \textbf{Clark's Nutcracker}, the gained [seed] goes to your personal supply unless you choose to cache it on this bird; caching is optional.

48173.duplicates: Existing \textbf{Montagu's Harrier} ruling: "Even when using this bird's power to play it on top of another bird, this bird may only be played in [grassland]." — covers question 2 only.
48173.note: Second half of the thread (\textbf{Montagu's Harrier} may only be played in [grassland]) is already covered by an existing ruling on that card. The general rule about teal powers spans all teal birds; cards list left empty because no teal bird was named in the thread.
48173.text: Teal ROUND END powers trigger at the end of every round after the bird is played, not only at the end of the round in which it was played (so up to 4 times per game).
48173.title: Round end powers

48556.note: Consistent with the existing \textbf{Falconer} ruling that colour is irrelevant; this ruling adds that the symbol must precede the power text.
48556.text: \textbf{Black-Billed Magpie} is not a [predator] bird and does not count toward the \textbf{Falconer} bonus card. It only triggers off other players' successful [predator] actions. A [predator] power is indicated by the [predator] symbol appearing before the power text, not within it.

48565.note: Answer covers both the bird-type question and the meaning of "succeeds"; could arguably be general (applies to all pink predator-trigger birds and to \textbf{Falconer}), but kept card-scoped per default.
48565.text: \textbf{Turkey Vulture} is not a [predator] bird; its [predator] symbol appears within the power text rather than before it. A predator ``succeeds'' when another player's [predator] power results in that player gaining a benefit — for example, revealing a card whose wingspan is less than the stated value and tucking it.

48825.note: The other bird in the thread (a Pesquet's Parrot-like power) was never named on a shown card, so the ruling is written generically about the trigger.
48825.text: \textbf{Spangled Drongo}'s power triggers whenever another player gains [nectar] by any means, not only when they gain it with the ``gain food'' action. For example, if another player gains 1 [nectar] from the supply through a bird power, \textbf{Spangled Drongo}'s owner may gain 1 [nectar] from the supply.

48916.note: Stated as a general premise for all bird powers requiring a specific food type; only Sandhill Crane was named.
48916.text: [nectar] cannot be substituted for a specific food type demanded by a bird power; a power such as \textbf{Sandhill Crane}'s ``Discard 1 [seed]'' must be paid with that food type.
48916.title: Nectar

49005.note: Answer is about the [wild] food symbol on a bird's food cost, not nests.
49005.text: A bird must have the [fish] symbol to count for \textbf{Fishery Manager}. A bird whose food cost shows only a [wild] symbol does not count.

49246.text: A bird with a [star] (wild) nest counts as having a [cavity] nest for \textbf{Blyth's Hornbill}, so you may discard all [egg] from a bird with a [star] nest.

49403.duplicates: You may not use this bird's power to lay an [egg] on another player's bird.
49403.reject_reason: Already covered by the existing Brown-Headed Cowbird ruling.

49407.duplicates: Even when using this bird's power to play it on top of another bird, this bird may only be played in [grassland].
49407.reject_reason: Already covered by an existing Montagu's Harrier ruling.

49408.duplicates: If this bird is played on top of a horizontal one (e.g., \textbf{Common Blackbird}), it is also placed horizontally and occupies both columns. / If a bird (e.g., \textbf{Common Buzzard}) is played on top of this one, the top bird is also placed horizontally and occupies both columns.
49408.reject_reason: Already covered by existing rulings on both the covering and sideways birds; the only new detail (it works the same whether or not a card sits to the right) is implicit in them.

49736.duplicates: Existing Green Heron ruling covers ``Trading'' counts as ``spending'' -- this is the complementary gain case, genuinely new.
49736.note: Jamey first answered the opposite (comment 49737) without the cards in front of him; Joe Aubrey corrected it, citing a ruling from designer Elizabeth Hargrave. The asker's ``Drongo'' is presumably Spangled Drongo (Oceania), but it was not named precisely enough to attach the ruling there.
49736.reject_reason: Green Heron already carries "When another player uses Green Heron's power to trade a food
49736.text: ``Trading'' one food for another, as with \textbf{Green Heron}, also counts as ``gaining'' the new food, so it triggers powers that activate when you gain that food type (e.g. gaining [nectar]).

49805.note: Jamey said "may be a typo in the appendix" but confirmed the bird is definitely when activated.
49805.text: \textbf{Budgerigar} is a brown ``when activated'' bird; the Oceania appendix listing it as ``when played'' is an error.

49900.text: \textbf{Loggerhead Shrike}'s power triggers only when another player takes the ``gain food'' action (activating their [forest] habitat). It does not trigger when another player gains [rodent] from a bird power such as \textbf{Grey Shrikethrush}.

49965.text: When [nectar] is used for this bird's ``any food'' power, place it on the ``spent nectar'' space for that habitat rather than discarding it to the supply.

50129.note: The thread's first question (comment 50132), that ``each player'' includes the hummingbird's owner and they may choose themselves first, duplicates the ruling proposed for thread 50685 (Ruby-Throated Hummingbird / Anna's Hummingbird).
50129.text: \textbf{Snow Bunting}'s power does not trigger during your own turn: if another player's ``once between turns'' power causes them to tuck a [card] while it is still your turn, it is not between your turns and \textbf{Snow Bunting} does not activate.

50137.note: The question described the power as an end-game bonus; the answer states the general principle that the [egg] limit always applies. Scoped to the card named.
50137.text: You are always limited by the [egg] limit of each bird, including when laying [egg] with an end-of-round or game-end power; if the birds in your [wetland] are already at their [egg] limit, no [egg] can be laid.

50436.text: Activate this power immediately when another player's [predator] succeeds, not at the end of that player's turn.

50484.note: Jamey phrased it as ``I would say it isn't in your supply, as your supply is off your mat.'' This appears to sit in tension with the existing \textbf{Coal Tit} ruling that you may spend cached [seed] anytime you can spend [seed] from your supply; reviewer should check how the two are presented together. Answer was specifically about the Nutcracker's ``from your supply'' wording.
50484.reject_reason: hedged, and contradicts the better ruling already on Coal Tit -- see rejections.json
50484.text: [seed] cached on \textbf{Coal Tit} is not in your personal supply, so it cannot be used for powers that cache or spend [seed] ``from your supply'', such as \textbf{Eurasian Nutcracker}'s power.

50502.duplicates: This bird counts double toward precisely the end-of-round bonuses that count birds, not those that count other quantities.
50502.reject_reason: Already covered by the existing ruling on both named cards.

50536.note: Related to the existing Rodentologist ruling (``Birds that eat [rodent]'', not ``only eat''), but that ruling does not address the [wild] symbol, so this is new content.
50536.text: A bird counts toward the \textbf{Rodentologist} bonus card only if it shows the [rodent] symbol; a [wild] (any food) symbol does not qualify.

50539.note: A second, unrelated question in the thread (comment 50547) confirms you gain food tokens one at a time and may reset the birdfeeder between them; that is a general birdfeeder rule not tied to these cards.
50539.text: You must discard an actual [fish] to activate \textbf{American White Pelican}; food substitutions only apply when playing a bird, not when paying a cost in a bird's power.

50676.note: Jamey initially answered incorrectly in comment 52558 (later edited) and confirmed the correct ruling in 52571. Also settled in the same thread (comment 50677): cards tucked by such powers are taken from the deck without looking, with no choice of which cards to tuck.
50676.text: When a bird power refers to a specific food type, [nectar] is not a wild food and cannot be substituted for it. For example, \textbf{Canada Goose} requires discarding a [seed]; [nectar] may not be discarded instead. [nectar] is wild only when paying food to play a bird, using an ``any food'' bird power, or upgrading an action.
50676.title: Nectar as a wild food

50685.note: The same thread also confirms (comment 50702) that a habitat with all 5 bird slots filled still gains the leftmost uncovered benefit -- the icons printed to the right of the 5th slot -- which is a board rule rather than a card ruling.
50685.text: ``The player of your choice'' includes all players, so the player activating \textbf{Ruby-Throated Hummingbird} may choose themselves to gain the first [die] from the birdfeeder.

51004.text: Zero birds counts as the fewest birds, so a player with no birds in their [wetland] can be the player with the fewest birds and draw 1 [card].

51030.note: The second sentence's point about activating the same bird twice in a turn is drawn from Jamey's worked example rather than stated as a rule.
51030.text: When a bird power refers to a characteristic of other birds, only birds currently on your player mat are applicable, not birds in your hand or elsewhere, unless the power specifically says otherwise (such as a power that looks at the top card of the deck). \textbf{Hooded Merganser} therefore repeats the power of a bird with the [predator] icon already played in its habitat, and a bird whose power it repeats may also be activated in its own right during the same turn as the action cube moves along the row.
51030.title: Powers referring to other birds

51304.duplicates: This bird's power activates another bird's brown power, and it may activate a bird's power regardless of whether that bird is to the left or right of this bird.
51304.note: Thread also mentions Grey Catbird, which was not shown among the cards but carries the same power text; a reviewer may wish to confirm the existing ruling is attached there too.
51304.reject_reason: Already covered by existing ruling on the repeat-power birds

51358.text: For the \textbf{birds with tucked [card]} end-of-round goal, count each of your birds with at least 1 card tucked beneath it. The [flocking] icon on the goal tile is synonymous with tucked cards; the powers of the birds involved are irrelevant, so it does not matter whether the bird has a [flocking] power or how the card came to be tucked there.
51358.title: Birds with tucked cards

51435.note: Answer given in the context of a teal European power but stated as a general principle for all powers.
51435.text: Activating any bird power is optional, including teal (round end) powers. A player may decline to activate a power, for example to avoid laying eggs on a bird when the end-of-round goal counts birds with no [egg].
51435.title: Powers

51599.duplicates: Partially overlaps the existing general ruling ``Regular reroll rules apply whenever you have the opportunity to gain food from the birdfeeder.''
51599.note: The thread also settled two other points: the ``Birds that eat berries'' bonus card (Fruit-based bonus) looks only for the [fruit] icon, so omnivores with that icon do count while birds without it do not; and \textbf{Bobolink}'s when-played power includes the just-played bird itself. Those may deserve separate rulings. This proposal covers only the birdfeeder-refresh timing.
51599.text: At any time when you are gaining food, you may refresh the birdfeeder if all dice in it show the same face; this includes between individual food gains and when only 1 die remains in the birdfeeder (a single die trivially shows all the same face). You may also gain fewer dice than the birdfeeder offers and refresh before choosing the next food.
51599.title: Rerolling dice

51702.note: The rulebook text quoted is on page 9. Thread also confirms the tray is normally fully reset only at the end of each round.
51702.text: As you draw face-up cards, they are not immediately refilled. Instead, wait until the end of your turn before refilling empty spaces on the bird tray. \textbf{Royal Spoonbill} allows you to reset (discard all cards on the tray and refill it) or refill the tray before drawing.
51702.title: Refilling the bird tray

51705.duplicates: If you use this bird's power to lay 2 [egg], they must be laid on different [ground]/[star] birds.
51705.reject_reason: Duplicates the existing Western Meadowlark ruling

51741.note: The thread's second question (the white ``no powers'' end-of-round goal counting birds with a ``when played'' power or no power) restates the European rulebook text and concerns a goal tile rather than a card, so it is not proposed separately.
51741.text: \textbf{Galah}'s tuck is not conditional on the chosen player gaining a [seed]: you tuck 2 [card] from the deck behind this bird even if the birdfeeder reset produces no [seed] for them.

51745.note: The answer also names the European Nuthatch, which was not listed among the thread's cards here but carries the identical power; a reviewer may wish to attach this ruling there too.
51745.text: Food cached on this bird counts as being in your supply only for the purpose of spending it. It is not actually in your supply for any other purpose, so it does not satisfy powers that check whether a player has a particular food in their supply.

51967.text: \textbf{Great Horned Owl}'s power says ``Look at a [card] from the deck,'' so it must use the top card of the deck; a face-up card from the tray may not be used. By contrast, a power that does not specify a source, such as \textbf{Forster's Tern}'s ``Draw 1 [card],'' lets you take either a face-up card or the top card of the deck.

52159.note: Jamey answered in two parts: comment 52329 (once between turns) and 52467 (a trade still counts as a gain). Source given is the later, decisive comment.
52159.text: When another player uses \textbf{Green Heron}'s power to trade a food token for [nectar], that counts as gaining [nectar], so \textbf{Spangled Drongo}'s power triggers. It is not a net gain of food, but it is still a gain. \textbf{Spangled Drongo} is a ``once between turns'' power, so it may only be used once between each of your turns.

52249.reject_reason: Misprinted card / replacement request, not a rules clarification.

52255.note: The answer is a general statement about discards, but only \textbf{Australian Ibis} was named. Could be promoted to a general ruling by a reviewer.
52255.text: Discarded bird cards and bonus cards are discarded face up, including the card discarded when using \textbf{Australian Ibis}'s power.

52266.duplicates: This bird counts toward the \textbf{Photographer} bonus card.
52266.note: Snow Bunting already carries a ruling that it counts toward Photographer; this thread only confirms it. The second question in the thread (no hand/food limit at end of turn) is basic rulebook content.
52266.text: \textbf{Snow Bunting} counts toward the \textbf{Photographer} bonus card, as \textit{snowy} is a qualifying keyword.

52560.note: Stated as a general principle by Jamey; applies to any power whose benefit cannot be fully realized.
52560.text: A power may be activated even if its full benefit is not possible; as much of it as possible is implemented. For example, \textbf{Lazuli Bunting}'s power may be used even if another player has no [bowl] bird with an empty nest to lay an [egg] on.
52560.title: Partial benefit

52686.note: Partially overlaps the existing ruling about which keywords qualify, but names two specific cases that ruling does not.
52686.text: \textit{Redstart} and \textit{yellowthroat} both count toward this bonus card; a full list of qualifying colors appears on page 4 of the Appendix.

52688.note: Answer given generally for migrating birds, but only Song Sparrow was named in the thread.
52688.text: This bird may move from any column, including the leftmost one, as long as there are no birds to the right of it in its row (Appendix, page 12).

52710.text: The 2-for-1 food conversion may only be used when paying the food cost to play a bird card. It cannot be used to supply the [invertebrate] discarded for this bird's power; you must discard actual [invertebrate].

52791.note: Note the existing general ruling that rerolls apply only when gaining food from the birdfeeder; Jamey extends the reroll allowance here because the power results in gaining food.
52791.text: When activating \textbf{Parrot Crossbill}, if all dice in the birdfeeder show the same face you may first refill the birdfeeder by rolling all dice, even though the [seed] is gained from the supply rather than from the die you remove.

52935.note: Reflects the general 'once between turns' timing rule, but stated here for these two specific cards.
52935.text: \textbf{Spangled Drongo} only triggers between your turns, never on your own turn. If you activate \textbf{Eastern Rosella} on your turn, causing all players to gain 1 [nectar], \textbf{Spangled Drongo} does not activate.

52959.note: Based on the Oceania reference tile order of operations: nectar is discarded in step 2, end-game powers occur later in round 6. Could arguably be generalised to all game-end powers, but the answer was given for this card.
52959.text: Nectar in your personal supply is returned to the supply during step 2 of the end of round 6, before ``game end'' powers such as \textbf{Grey-Headed Mannikin}'s are activated, so that nectar is no longer available to help pay the food cost of the bird played with this power.

53058.note: Question was about the Photographer bonus card specifically; the answer restates how all bonus card scoring brackets work, but keeping it card-scoped as asked.
53058.text: The point values on this bonus card are totals, not per-bird: if you have the number of qualifying birds shown, you gain that number of points in total.

53260.duplicates: The Mute Swan and Eleonora's Falcon missing-icon answers are already covered by existing rulings on those cards.
53260.note: Jamey's wording (``no, it isn't missing the predator icon'') is slightly ambiguous but in context means Little Owl correctly has no predator icon. Reviewer may wish to confirm before publishing.
53260.reject_reason: Jamey Stegmaier's answer is a double negative -- "no, it isn't missing the predator icon"
53260.text: \textbf{Little Owl} does not have a [predator] power, and its card is not missing a [predator] icon; it does not count for the \textbf{Falconer} bonus card.

53411.note: Jamey phrases it as a global rule ("I think it's a global rule in Wingspan"), and adds that for \textbf{Indian Peafowl} the order does not matter since the draw is random. Marked general because it governs any multi-player-choice power; the two cards named here are attached.
53411.text: Unless a card states otherwise, when a power involves multiple players making a choice, the current player chooses first and the choice proceeds clockwise around the table.
53411.title: Turn order for choices

53444.reject_reason: Request for a bird in a future expansion; no rules content.

53487.note: Jamey answered the general ordering principle without the cards in front of him (``generally you can choose the order in which cards activate''); the worked consequence for these two teal birds was spelled out by a non-official commenter. The consequence follows directly from the official answer, but a reviewer may prefer to trim the second sentence.
53487.text: Round end powers are activated one at a time, in an order you choose, each fully resolved before the next. With both \textbf{Lesser Whitethroat} and \textbf{Black Redstart} on your mat, the first one you activate lays [egg] on each bird in a habitat with no [egg]; the second can then only activate if you still have a habitat with no [egg].

53612.duplicates: This bird counts double toward precisely the end-of-round bonuses that count birds, not those that count other quantities.
53612.reject_reason: Already covered by the existing Greylag Goose ruling that it counts double only for end-of-round goals that count birds.

53773.text: \textbf{Ethologist} scores in a single habitat of your choice: choose one habitat (row), ignore the other two, and score 2 points for each different power color present in that row. Multiple birds of the same color in that row score only once for that color. For example, a row with 2 brown, 1 white, and 1 pink bird scores 6 points.

54053.note: The question describes Red-Crowned Crane (score a bonus card, discard it) without naming it; the Asia page thread context and card text confirm the bird.
54053.text: A bonus card discarded to score \textbf{Red-Crowned Crane} goes to the discarded bonus card pile and may be retrieved later with \textbf{Wrybill}, allowing the same bonus card to be scored twice.

54085.reject_reason: General chat about disc golf, no rules content.

54199.reject_reason: About promo card availability/design history, not a rules clarification.

54302.note: Balance discussion in the thread is opinion and not included. Wording note: a Wingspan column spans the three habitats at the same slot position.
54302.text: For \textbf{Behaviorist}, a column is a straight stack of card slots within a single row position across the three habitats. The birds with 3 different power colors must all be in the same column; colors matched diagonally or in other arrangements do not count.

54463.text: With \textbf{Kea}, you first draw 1 bonus card, then decide how many additional cards you want to draw and discard the corresponding amount of [wild]. This is a one-time decision, so you cannot discard food one at a time. Among all the bonus cards drawn using this bird's power, you keep only 1.

54522.note: The thread's first exchange is a digital-app bug report, which is not a ruling. The quoted wording of Masked Lapwing in the question differs slightly from the printed card, but the substance (gain 1 per food type in the birdfeeder) matches.
54522.text: When using \textbf{Masked Lapwing}'s power, a die showing two food types (such as a [nectar] face) counts as both types: gain 1 of each type shown, up to a maximum of 1 of each type overall.

54599.note: Quotes page 2 of the Oceania rulebook. The removal suggestion is an optional variant, not a rule. \textbf{Galah} was mentioned only in a community strategy comment, so it is not attached.
54599.text: The [wild] symbol always includes [nectar], so \textbf{Chihuahuan Raven} and \textbf{Common Raven} may take [nectar] from the supply with their powers. The Oceania rulebook suggests that players who find this too powerful remove those two birds from the deck when playing with the Oceania Expansion.

54616.note: Jamey's first reply (54617) guessed wrong based on a hunting-power premise; comment 54620 is the corrected answer after the card text was quoted.
54616.text: \textbf{Galah}'s tuck is not conditional on the other player's result: you tuck 2 [card] behind this bird whether or not the reset birdfeeder contains a [seed] for them to gain.

54634.note: The question asked about an end-of-round goal; Jamey's answer says ``end-game scoring''. Ruling written to cover counting birds in the habitat generally, which is the substance of the answer.
54634.text: A bird played sideways across 2 [wetland] spaces, such as \textbf{Grey Heron}, is still only one bird card and counts once toward goals and scoring that count birds in a habitat.

54692.note: Confirms page 11 of the Oceania rulebook.
54692.text: \textbf{Wrybill} counts as pointing left for goals and bonus cards that care about bill direction: although the bird is facing straight ahead, its bill points toward the left side of the card. What matters is the bill, not the bird's face.

54779.reject_reason: Speculation about unreleased product; official answer deferred

54913.duplicates: This bird counts double toward precisely the end-of-round bonuses that count birds, not those that count other quantities.
54913.note: Largely covered by the existing ruling on this card; the only new content is the explicit ``filled columns'' example. Reviewer may prefer to fold that example into the existing ruling rather than add a row.
54913.text: \textbf{Eurasian Green Woodpecker} counts double only toward end-of-round goals that count birds, if it qualifies. It does not count as an extra filled column for the ``filled columns'' goal.

54944.note: The answer addresses Snow Bunting specifically; the same ``Do X, then if you do, Y'' principle already exists in the corpus as the conditional carve-out, but this thread only settles Snow Bunting.
54944.text: \textbf{Snow Bunting}'s power uses ``then,'' so you must tuck a [card] from your hand to gain the ``draw 1 [card]'' benefit.

55083.text: The number of [card] you draw with \textbf{Hooded Crow}'s power is equal to the number of [card] you tuck; you must tuck in order to draw.

55106.note: Jamey only queried the premise (there is a single Common Starling in the game); no ruling given.
55106.reject_reason: Official reply asked for clarification and did not resolve the question

55181.duplicates: Existing House Wren ruling: "When using this bird's power, the additional bird must be played in the same habitat as this bird."
55181.text: The additional bird played with \textbf{House Wren}'s power must be played in the same habitat as \textbf{House Wren} itself, even though \textbf{House Wren} may be played in either of two habitats.

55198.duplicates: Existing (Rose-Breasted Grosbeak): "When using this bird's power, if all [die] in the birdfeeder show the same face you may reroll before taking food."; general: "Regular reroll rules apply whenever you have the opportunity to gain food from the birdfeeder."
55198.note: Jamey's initial answer (comment 55201) said the opposite for ``if available'' powers and was corrected/edited; Joe Aubrey's comment 55217 is the settling answer. The immediate-refill-of-an-empty-birdfeeder point comes from comment 55203 in the same thread. Partly duplicates the existing Rose-Breasted Grosbeak ruling and the general "Rerolling dice" ruling, but adds the explicit ``if available'' coverage.
55198.text: You may always reroll the birdfeeder when you are going to it to gain food and all [die] in the tray show the same face (including if there is only one [die]). This includes powers that look for a specific food ``if available.'' An empty birdfeeder is refilled immediately, rather than waiting until someone needs to gain food.
55198.title: Rerolling dice

55230.reject_reason: Request for future birds; points to a submission form

55246.reject_reason: General chat and expansion-content commentary; no rules question resolved (only a pointer to the rulebook and a note that the dice are unchanged).

55254.note: The thread also confirms Asia adds no new end-of-round goals for the core game (only Duet mode goals); that part is not a card ruling and is omitted.
55254.text: A ``neighbor'' in Wingspan is defined as the players to your immediate left and right, not all players at the table.
55254.title: Neighbors

55304.reject_reason: Flock mode setup/logistics advice; the answer does not settle a rules question (piles are 'effectively one deck', arrangement is only for convenience)

55514.reject_reason: Enthusiasm and product/box packing chat, no rules content

55543.note: Jamey hedges slightly (``As far as I can tell''). Grassland Data Analyst is a bonus card not listed among the thread's cards here, but is named in the question; only Emu and Large Bird Specialist listed. General scope because it covers all [star]-wingspan birds (Emu, Ostrich, etc.) and all wingspan bonus cards.
55543.text: Birds with a [star] (wild) wingspan have a wild wingspan for each individual bonus card, similar to how a [wild] nest can act as multiple nest types for bonuses, goals, and powers. For example, \textbf{Emu} can simultaneously count as a mid-sized wingspan for \textbf{Grassland Data Analyst} and as a wingspan over 65 cm for \textbf{Large Bird Specialist}.
55543.title: Wild wingspan

55604.duplicates: This bird's power is triggered by another player playing a bird in their [forest] during their turn...
55604.reject_reason: The [OFFICIAL] reply only asked for the card text; the answer given was from a non-official commenter, and the point is already covered by the existing Eastern Kingbird ruling.

55913.note: The underlying principle ([wild] always includes [nectar]) is stated in the Oceania rulebook; kept card-scoped since the thread only settles the caching case for this bird.
55913.text: The [wild] (``any food'') symbol always includes [nectar], so you may cache [nectar] with this bird's power if you still have [nectar] in your supply when the round-end power activates.

56518.note: Thread also contains a translation question (comment 56522), which is not a ruling.
56518.text: The first time you activate \textbf{Great Cormorant}, ignore the first clause (there is no [fish] on the bird yet) and skip right to rolling 2 [die]. On later activations, move 1 [fish] to your supply if one is cached there; if not, again skip straight to rolling 2 [die].

56607.note: Asked in the context of placing a duet token on a food die bonus space (Asia duet map). The answer is stated as a general principle about the [die] symbol; the Bird Feeder bonus card is the only card named in the thread and its relevance is indirect, so a reviewer may prefer to attach this to duet map / birdfeeder contexts instead.
56607.text: The food [die] symbol always means, ``Remove a die from the birdfeeder and gain the food noted on it from the supply.''
56607.title: Food die

56612.note: The thread asks about all three Ranger bonus cards (Forest, Grassland, Wetland); only Wetland Ranger's text was shown. Reviewer should confirm the exact names of the other two before attaching.
56612.text: Tied scores do not count as ascending or descending—5 is not higher than 5—so a run of birds worth 5, 5, 3, 3, 3 points does not form an ascending or descending sequence.

56682.reject_reason: Component/packing question (extra duplicate card), not a rules clarification.

56766.text: The second sentence of \textbf{Sri Lanka Frogmouth}'s power is not dependent on the first: all players may discard 1 [card] to gain 1 [invertebrate] regardless of whether the die roll succeeded.

56858.note: Note the tension with ruling 20200404 ("you can take less of an action beneficial to yourself") -- that principle concerns partially taking resources for yourself, whereas this answer concerns powers that also benefit opponents. Reviewer may want to reconcile the wording.
56858.text: Activating a bird's power is always optional, but if you choose to activate it, the entire power resolves; you may not use only the part of the power you like and ignore the rest. In particular, you may decline to activate \textbf{Hermit Thrush}, but if you do activate it, the player(s) with the fewest birds in their [forest] gain their [die].
56858.title: Activating a power is all-or-nothing

56860.note: Applies to all birds whose power says ``Roll any X [die]''; only Eurasian Kestrel was named in the thread.
56860.text: When a power tells you to roll ``any'' dice, you choose where those dice come from (birdfeeder or table). The dice you roll are placed on the table.
56860.title: Rolling ``any'' dice

56984.note: Thread also contains a confirmed clarification that end-of-round goals count everything accumulated so far in the game, not only what happened during the round just ended (comment 56985), and that "draw a card" defaults to a choice of the bird tray or the top of the deck (comments 56989/57000) -- the latter is already covered by an existing American Oystercatcher ruling. The card list here is only the card named in the thread; the drawn-cards-enter-your-hand rule spans all birds with "draw ... then discard" powers and needs a predicate.
56984.text: Whenever you draw [card], they enter your hand immediately. Cards you have just drawn are therefore eligible when a power instructs you to discard a [card] from your hand.
56984.title: Drawn cards enter your hand

57074.note: Officially phrased as a general principle covering benefits granted to non-active players; only \textbf{Brolga} is named in the thread.
57074.text: Any player may decline a benefit, whether it comes from their own power or from another player's power. With \textbf{Brolga}, the chosen player may decline to lay the [egg], and you still draw 2 [card] either way. Having food stolen is not a benefit, so a player being stolen from has no choice.
57074.title: Declining a benefit

57119.reject_reason: Component/contents and rulebook-scope questions about Wingspan Asia; no rules clarification.

57127.note: Could arguably support a note that Anatomist, Cartographer and Photographer were reprinted with new keywords in Wingspan Asia, but existing rulings on those cards already cover the keyword lists.
57127.reject_reason: Component/printing information and a recommendation about which bonus card to leave out; not a rules clarification.

57138.note: Same principle as thread 56984 (Jamey's answer about American Oystercatcher and "draw a card" by default). Existing American Oystercatcher ruling already covers that card specifically.
57138.text: Unless a power specifies that cards must be drawn from the deck or from the bird tray, you may choose where to draw each [card] from: the face-up cards in the bird tray or the top of the deck. On \textbf{Indian Peafowl}, the additional [card] you draw may come from either source, even though the first 2 [card] must come from the deck.
57138.title: Where you draw from

57142.note: If Duet Map rulings are in scope, the ruling would be: you may place a duet token on a food space only for food you actually spent, and paying part of Bonelli's Eagle's [rodent] cost with a real [rodent] does allow claiming a [rodent] duet space (comment 57611).
57142.reject_reason: About Duet Map token placement, a separate expansion component not covered by card pages; the Bonelli's Eagle content is only that food actually spent lets you claim that food's duet token.

57163.note: The thread's later exchange (comments 57328/57329) repeats the \textbf{Great Cormorant} first-fish question already covered by thread 56518.
57163.text: With \textbf{Plumbeous Redstart}, the other players keep the [card] they drew only if that card has a [invertebrate] or [seed] in its food cost; it is not the card you drew that determines this. Despite the different wording, the power works the same way as \textbf{Little Egret}.

57347.note: Two official comments (57348 and 57644) build the same ruling; 57644 is the one settling the ``any dice'' choice. Could arguably be general across all Asia ``roll any X dice'' powers, but only Great Cormorant was named.
57347.text: For powers that let you roll ``any'' dice, such as \textbf{Great Cormorant}, you may roll dice that are inside the birdfeeder, outside the birdfeeder, or a mix of both. Dice you take from the birdfeeder remain out of the birdfeeder after rolling, until the birdfeeder is refilled.

57377.text: When \textbf{Plumbeous Redstart} is activated, the other players must reveal the [card] they draw to prove whether it has a [invertebrate] or [seed] in its food cost.

57386.note: Jamey answered before seeing the card text, so the answer is a general statement about Duet tokens applied to the described situation rather than a card-specific verdict. The follow-up question about combining expansions without the base game was not answered.
57386.text: In Duet mode, moving this bird to another player's mat does not affect Duet tokens: Duet tokens are only placed by the player who plays a bird card, so only that player pays the costs and gains the benefits.

57392.note: The referenced duet-mode answer is not present in the thread, so no self-contained ruling can be extracted.
57392.reject_reason: Answer refers to an unstated earlier duet-mode answer; nothing resolved in this thread.

57443.text: The 2 resources other players discard to draw 2 new bonus cards and keep 1 must come from their personal supply; cached food on birds may not be discarded for this.

57449.note: Answer is confusing and resolves nothing durable about gameplay. The existing Photographer misprint-style rulings already cover corrected-card matters.
57449.reject_reason: Component/printing question about replacement bonus cards; the answer about the point value is also internally inconsistent (asks about 6 vs 7, replies '7 points is how the card was printed').

57513.note: Jamey confirmed the asker's interpretation in full; the same reasoning presumably applies to other Asia dice-rolling powers, but only Forest Owlet was named.
57513.text: The dice chosen for this bird's power are rolled outside the birdfeeder. If choosing them empties the birdfeeder, all 5 [die] are rerolled into the birdfeeder (resetting it) once the rolling is complete, before play continues.

57608.text: Because caching is optional, you may instead add the [seed] gained with \textbf{Red-Bellied Woodpecker}'s power to your personal food supply.

57620.note: The bonus card referred to is \textbf{Bird Feeder}/\textbf{Behaviorist}-style; the questioner described 'the bonus card that gives 3 points for each bird that allows you to score or draw bonus cards'. Wording kept generic since the specific bonus card was not named.
57620.text: \textbf{Rose-Ringed Parakeet} does not count for bonus cards that reward birds allowing you to score or draw bonus cards, even if its copied ``When Played'' power (such as \textbf{Bell's Vireo}'s) draws bonus cards, because its own power is not specific to drawing bonus cards.

57636.note: The thread's first question (turn order/round structure) is basic rulebook explanation and not proposed as a ruling; the ruling comes from the later, unrelated question in the same thread.
57636.text: When scoring a bonus card immediately with \textbf{Red-Crowned Crane}, ignore any ``at game end'' wording on the bonus card and score it based on the current game state. For \textbf{Winter Feeder}, score based on the food currently in your personal supply.

57683.note: The shown text for Small Minivet/Trumpeter Finch lists ``1 [invertebrate] or 1 [egg]'' and ``1 [seed] or 1 [egg]''; the thread discusses ignoring an invertebrate or seed. Ruling kept generic about ``the food types named on the bird'' to avoid contradicting either version.
57683.text: The text printed on \textbf{Small Minivet} and \textbf{Trumpeter Finch} takes precedence over the general wording in the appendix: only the food types named on the bird itself may be ignored in the cost of the additional bird.

57695.note: Thread also contains an eco-friendly components question (comments 57699/57701), which is not a rules matter. Closely related to the existing Yellowhammer ruling about resolving the new teal power among your remaining teal powers, but this comment states explicitly that the newly played bird's power may be used.
57695.text: If you use \textbf{Yellowhammer}'s power to play a bird with a round-end (teal) power, you may activate that newly played bird's power, as long as you are still in the round-end power activation step.

57710.text: \textbf{Blue Grosbeak}'s power may be used every time it is activated, as long as no other bird in its habitat is to its right; it may be moved again to a different habitat on a later turn.

57713.note: The answer confirms the changed point value is official but does not state which tier changed; the questioner reported 7 points down to 6. Reviewer may want to check the exact scoring tiers before publishing.
57713.text: The version of this bonus card printed in the Asia expansion awards 6 points instead of 7 for the higher tier. Although unintended, that is the official version of the card.

57715.text: For \textbf{Forest Ranger}, birds with equal scores do not continue a sequence, since a score is not higher (or lower) than an identical score. Scores of 1-2-2-3-5 in [forest] count as a sequence of three, not five.

57766.note: Question raised in the context of combining expansions (e.g., \textbf{Horsfield's Bronze-Cuckoo}, which has a 0-egg limit); the answer is stated generally for any 0-egg-limit bird.
57766.text: This bird's power may be used to lay an [egg] on a bird with an egg limit of 0, since it allows going 2 over the egg limit.

57768.duplicates: If you use this bird's power to copy the power of a bird that lets it move to another habitat---and this bird satisfies applicable conditions (e.g., being the rightmost bird in its habitat)---this bird may move to that habitat, even one in which it cannot be played.
57768.reject_reason: Already covered by an existing Superb Lyrebird ruling.

57777.duplicates: If this bird is played on top of a horizontal one (e.g., \textbf{Common Blackbird}), it is also placed horizontally and occupies both columns. / (European Roller) If a bird (e.g., \textbf{Common Buzzard}) is played on top of this one, the top bird is also placed horizontally and occupies both columns.
57777.reject_reason: Already covered by existing rulings on Montagu's Harrier, Common Buzzard, and European Roller.

57789.reject_reason: Concerns Duet mode tokens/map, which wingsearch does not cover.

57800.note: Refines the existing “``Trading'' counts as ``spending''” ruling with the nectar-specific consequence.
57800.text: When you use this bird's power to trade [nectar] for another food type, the [nectar] is spent, so place it in the spent-nectar space of that habitat rather than returning it to the supply.

57954.note: Golden Pheasant is only mentioned as an example in a Duet map question; its shown power text is unrelated to the answer.
57954.reject_reason: Duet mode / Duet map setup and scoring; not a card or general gameplay ruling wingsearch carries.

57990.note: Answer was given as a principle about dice-rolling powers in general; scoped here to the three Asia birds named in the thread.
57990.text: Where a power says to roll ``any'' dice, you may choose whether the dice come from the birdfeeder or from outside it. Either way, dice rolled for a bird power stay out of the birdfeeder.

57999.text: The [rodent] discarded for \textbf{Korimako}'s power come from your own personal supply, not from the birdfeeder. Throughout the rulebook, ``discard'' refers to paying food from your supply.

58044.note: Jamey confirms either version may be played but officially the newest printing (6 points) governs.
58044.text: The \textbf{Anatomist} bonus card was reprinted in the Asia expansion with 6 points instead of 7 for 4+ birds. The change was unintentional, but the most recent version of the card is the official one.

58253.text: \textbf{Great Indian Bustard} caches [seed] equal to the bonus card's value at the time it is played (each cached [seed] is worth 1 point at game end), and the same bonus card is also scored normally at game end based on its condition at that time. For example, with \textbf{Visionary Leader} and 6 [card] in hand when the Bustard is played, cache 4 [seed]; at game end score \textbf{Visionary Leader} again for the [card] then in hand.

58894.note: Two cards clarified in one answer; mostly restates card text, but confirms the first sentence of Great Cormorant may be skipped when no fish is cached. Reviewer may wish to split into two card rulings.
58894.text: \textbf{Great Cormorant}'s first sentence is skipped if there is no [fish] cached on this bird; you will usually only have a [fish] to move on later activations, after caching one with the second sentence. \textbf{Red-Wattled Lapwing} lets you discard any number of [card] from the tray and refill it, laying 1 [egg] on this bird if at least 1 of the discarded birds is a [predator] (indicated by the skull and crossbones symbol).

59146.duplicates: Existing Southern Cassowary ruling: "When using this bird's power to discard another bird from your mat, all food cached on that bird, [egg] laid on that bird, and [card] tucked under that bird are discarded."
59146.note: Fully covered by the existing ruling on this card.
59146.reject_reason: Southern Cassowary already carries "When using this bird's power to discard another bird
59146.text: When \textbf{Southern Cassowary} discards a bird from your [forest] to take its place, any [egg] and cached food on the discarded bird are lost.

59161.note: Endangered Species is a Swift Start / promo bonus card and may not be in the database; the ruling is attached to Visionary Leader, which is named in the thread. The broader premise (cards referring to bird cards mean played birds unless stated otherwise) could justify a general ruling, but only these two cards were discussed.
59161.text: The \textbf{Endangered Species} bonus card counts only birds you have played on your player mat. Birds in hand that score for \textbf{Visionary Leader} do not count for \textbf{Endangered Species}, since cards that refer to bird cards look only at played birds unless stated otherwise.

59165.note: Also in this thread: Jamey first said a sequence of 10/23/23/30 scores as a sequence of 2 for the habitat Data Analyst bonus cards (comment 59166), then retracted it in comment 59200, confirming the appendix rule that ``a sequence may include two or more birds with the same wingspan''. No ruling proposed for that since the official position is the printed appendix text. The nectar-reset ruling is a general birdfeeder/nectar timing rule not tied to any named card; cards list left empty as no card is involved.
59165.reject_reason: no card to attach to (Oceania mat bonus) -- see rejections.json
59165.text: With only 1 [die] left in the birdfeeder, a [nectar] is not needed to reset it, so spending [nectar] for that purpose is not allowed.
59165.title: Resetting the birdfeeder with [nectar]

59296.note: Thread also contains a separate question (comment 59316) about copying a brown power, which is covered by the existing general 'Copy'-style rulings; only the first Q&A is proposed here.
59296.text: \textbf{Wilson's Storm Petrel}'s power requires you to end the turn with at least 1 of the [card] you drew with it, but any of the others may be disposed of in other ways during the turn (for example, tucked with \textbf{Common Grackle}) instead of being discarded.

59318.text: For \textbf{Common Tailorbird}, ``contiguous'' means orthogonally adjacent: directly to the left, right, top, or bottom, never diagonal. The group may zig-zag across rows and columns as long as each bird in the group is orthogonally adjacent to at least one other bird in the group.

59319.text: A bonus card discarded via \textbf{Red-Crowned Crane} cannot be scored at game end, so \textbf{Great Indian Bustard}'s instruction to ``also score it normally at game end'' no longer applies to that bonus card.

59530.text: \textbf{Ethologist} scores 2 points for each \textit{distinct} power color present in the chosen habitat, not 2 points per bird. Four brown-powered birds and one white-powered bird in the same habitat score 4 points, because the four brown birds count as only one color.

59657.note: Duet mode is an Asia expansion (2-player duet map) mechanic; not solo/Automa.
59657.text: Duet tokens are only placed when you play a bird, so no one places a duet token when \textbf{Blue Rock-Thrush} or \textbf{Spotted Dove} moves to another player's mat. If a bird is later played on that space, a duet token is placed as normal.

59700.duplicates: Regular reroll rules apply whenever you have the opportunity to gain food from the birdfeeder.
59700.note: Closely related to the existing general ruling ``Regular reroll rules apply whenever you have the opportunity to gain food from the birdfeeder,'' but this adds the specific case of a single non-matching die with \textbf{Emu}; reviewer may prefer to treat it as a duplicate.
59700.text: Whenever you go to the birdfeeder to gain food, for any reason, you may reroll the dice if all the faces are the same. So when \textbf{Emu} is activated and only a single die remains in the birdfeeder, you may reroll it even if it is not showing [seed].

59780.text: \textbf{Black-Shouldered Kite}'s power lays all 3 [egg] at once as part of resolving the power, essentially ``lay 3 [egg] on this bird if you can''; eggs already on the bird may limit its remaining egg capacity.

59932.note: The same thread also contains comment 60775 confirming \textbf{Barrow's Goldeneye} counts for \textbf{Photographer}, which is already covered by the existing Photographer keyword-list ruling.
59932.text: You look at the first bonus card drawn with \textbf{Kea}'s power before deciding how many additional bonus cards to draw. Deciding how many additional cards to draw, and discarding the corresponding amount of [wild], is a one-time decision. Among all the bonus cards drawn with this power, you keep only 1.

60158.text: For \textbf{Hermit Thrush}, zero counts as ``fewest'': player(s) with no birds in their [forest] gain 1 [die] from the birdfeeder.

60596.duplicates: The only keywords that qualify a bird to count toward this bonus card are those listed thereon, including \textit{prairie} ..., and those in the relevant sections of the expansion rulebooks.
60596.reject_reason: Already covered by the existing Cartographer ruling on expansion rulebook keyword lists.

60605.text: When \textbf{Large-Billed Crow} caches [nectar], place it on the bird, not in your personal supply of spent [nectar].

60643.note: The thread also includes comment 60651 on word-based bonus cards (\textbf{Photographer}, \textbf{Anatomist}) --- that is already covered by the existing keyword-list rulings on those bonus cards, except for the note that the Wingspan Asia \textbf{Photographer} lists ``bronze'', ``gold'' and ``silver''.
60643.text: \textbf{Rose-Ringed Parakeet} copies the power exactly as worded on the neighbor's bird onto itself for the duration of that turn only; at the end of the turn it no longer has that power. Copying \textbf{Bonelli's Eagle} or \textbf{Eastern Imperial Eagle} does nothing, since those powers refer to [rodent] in the bird's cost and \textbf{Rose-Ringed Parakeet} costs no [rodent]. Because the copied power is gone by the end of the turn, a copied bonus-card power does not make \textbf{Rose-Ringed Parakeet} count toward the \textbf{Endangered Species} bonus card when scoring at game end.

60699.duplicates: The only keywords that qualify a bird to count toward this bonus card are those listed thereon and those in the relevant sections of the expansion rulebooks.
60699.reject_reason: Restates an existing ruling (only keywords listed on the bonus card count) and concerns a French-language card name.

60790.note: Consistent with the existing \textbf{Photographer} ruling on substrings that do not refer to colors.
60790.text: \textbf{Baya Weaver} does not count toward the \textbf{Photographer} bonus card. That card looks for colors as words or as part of compound words, and ``Baya'' is its own word, not a compound of ``bay'' and ``a''.

60898.note: Jamey's first answer (comment 60906) was wrong and he corrected himself in comment 61154; the corrected answer is used. Answer is scoped to ``any food''/[wild] powers generally, but only Green Heron was named.
60898.text: [nectar] is an eligible food type for \textbf{Green Heron}'s power, so you may trade 1 [wild] for [nectar] from the supply. (An earlier official answer saying nectar was ineligible was retracted.)

60928.note: Two official comments: 60932 restates the Wingspan Asia FAQ entry about the first fish; 60934 settles which dice are rolled and that they leave the birdfeeder. Both are combined here; 60934 cited as it is the newly settled part. A reviewer may wish to split the 'roll any 2 dice' half into a general ruling for other Asia birds with that wording.
60928.text: When a power says ``roll any 2 [die]'', you choose which dice to roll, whether from inside or outside the birdfeeder, and the dice you roll are taken out of the birdfeeder. The first time you activate \textbf{Great Cormorant} there is no [fish] on it, so ignore the first clause and go straight to rolling 2 [die]; do the same on any later activation when the bird has no [fish] cached on it.

61022.note: The answer is phrased generally about bonus cards that name a specific food icon, but only Viticulturalist was named.
61022.text: \textbf{Viticulturalist} counts only birds showing the [fruit] icon; [wild] and [nectar] icons do not count for it.

61074.note: The answer covers all Ranger bonus cards (Forest, Grassland, Wetland Ranger), but only Forest Ranger was named in the thread; a reviewer may wish to extend it to the other Ranger cards.
61074.text: The Ranger bonus cards use the strict definitions of ascending and descending, so repeated point values break the series (unlike the \textbf{Data Analyst} bonus card, which explicitly allows equal wingspans). With scores of 6, 5, 5, 4, 3 in [forest], \textbf{Forest Ranger} scores only the longest strictly ascending or descending series: 5, 4, 3.

61551.text: \textbf{Cetti's Warbler}'s power applies only to the bird card itself, not to its duet token. Place a single duet token when you play \textbf{Cetti's Warbler}, just as with any other bird.

61800.text: \textbf{Spangled Drongo}'s power triggers when another player gains [nectar] in any way, including gaining [nectar] from the supply by discarding [fruit] with \textbf{Mistletoebird}'s power.

62306.text: \textbf{Hooded Merganser}'s power is activated as a brown power, so it can only repeat another brown power -- specifically a [predator] power.

62522.note: Answer was explicitly stated as a general principle for all abilities that look at bird types; only Carrion Crow is named in the thread.
62522.text: Powers that refer to types of birds (e.g., \textbf{Carrion Crow}, which caches 1 [rodent] for each [predator] a player has) always refer to birds played on a player mat, never to birds in hand.
62522.title: Bird types

62526.note: Duet tokens are an Asia expansion mechanic; the ruling concerns playing this European bird while using the duet map.
62526.text: Although \textbf{Common Blackbird} is placed sideways and covers 2 [forest] spaces, playing it still only allows you to place 1 duet token on the duet map.

62564.text: If there is no [fish] on this bird when its power is activated, ignore the first clause and skip straight to rolling 2 [die]; the clause about moving 1 [fish] from this bird to your supply only applies once a [fish] has been cached there.

62578.note: Thread carries three separate questions: all-players-lay-an-egg (comment 62580, which restates the standard rule that optional effects for other players are their choice), the House Wren habitat question (comment 62588, already covered by the existing House Wren ruling ``the additional bird must be played in the same habitat as this bird''), and this nectar question.
62578.text: Nectar discarded to \textbf{Eurasian Collared-Dove}'s power goes to the left side of your player mat (where discarded nectar is kept until the end of the game), not back to the supply. Round-end powers are resolved before nectar is discarded at the end of the round.

62823.duplicates: (Greylag Goose) ... When in your hand this card does not count toward end-of-round bonuses.
62823.note: Also duplicates the general ruling 'Only powers of birds played on a player mat can be used.'
62823.reject_reason: Already covered by existing Greylag Goose ruling (and the general 'Powers' ruling).

62835.note: The question mentioned a two-player game, but the answer is not restricted to player count.
62835.text: You may choose yourself as the starting player for this bird's power.

63044.note: Compare the existing \textbf{Eurasian Nuthatch} ruling about \textbf{Superb Lyrebird}, which says the copying bird retains the ability to spend the cached [seed] until end of turn. This answer is stricter for \textbf{Northern Mockingbird}; a reviewer may want to reconcile the two.
63044.text: When \textbf{Northern Mockingbird} repeats the power of \textbf{Eurasian Nuthatch}, the [seed] gained is cached on \textbf{Northern Mockingbird} but cannot later be spent; it is only copying the power when activated, so the [seed] simply remains cached food worth 1 VP at the end of the game.

63070.note: Answer is about Duet map token placement and the reset space; no clarification about the named birds' powers themselves.
63070.reject_reason: Duet Mode (Asia) map/token rules, not a card ruling wingsearch covers

63495.note: Jamey notes a digital implementation may handle the empty-deck case differently; the ruling above is for the analog game. The thread discusses tucking from the deck generally, but only European Goldfinch was named.
63495.text: If the deck runs out, shuffle the discard pile to form a new deck. If absolutely no cards remain in the game, there is nothing to tuck and powers such as \textbf{European Goldfinch}'s that tuck from the deck cannot be used. Tucked cards are effectively counters: nothing on the other side of a tucked card matters for gameplay, but they are real bird cards removed from the deck.

63579.note: The official answer is phrased as a general principle about [star] wingspans, but only \textbf{Budgerigar} was discussed; kept card-scoped.
63579.text: A bird with a [star] wingspan may be treated as any wingspan you choose at the moment it matters, so when activating \textbf{Budgerigar} you may decide whether a [star] bird in the tray counts as the smallest bird.

63945.duplicates: General ruling ``You may activate each `once between turns' power on a bird on your player mat once between each of your turns.''
63945.note: Card-specific illustration of the existing general once-between-turns ruling.
63945.reject_reason: Turkey Vulture already carries the general ruling "You may activate each 'once between
63945.text: \textbf{Turkey Vulture}'s power may only be used once between your turns, so if an opponent activates two successful [predator] powers during a single turn, you still gain only 1 food.

63979.duplicates: Existing general ruling ``Regular reroll rules apply whenever you have the opportunity to gain food from the birdfeeder.'' partially covers the reroll-while-caching part.
63979.note: Thread bundles three answers: simultaneous pink power ordering (turn order after active player), pink predator-triggered powers resolving before the active player's next bird, and rerolling when caching. The reroll portion largely duplicates the existing general reroll ruling; a reviewer may wish to split this into separate rulings. Automa/solo not involved.
63979.text: When several players' ``once between turns'' powers are triggered at the same time, they resolve in turn order, starting with the player after the active player. \textbf{Black Vulture}, \textbf{Black-Billed Magpie} and \textbf{Turkey Vulture} are triggered and activated as soon as the successful [predator] finishes its power, before the active player continues to their next bird, so those players go to the birdfeeder before the active player's remaining birds are activated. You may reroll the birdfeeder whenever you go to it to gain food for any reason, including caching, if all dice show the same face.

64069.reject_reason: Speculation about future changes to the Historian bonus card and bird names; no rules clarification.

64166.duplicates: Rerolling dice: "Regular reroll rules apply whenever you have the opportunity to gain food from the birdfeeder." (partially covers this)
64166.note: Overlaps the existing general ruling "Regular reroll rules apply whenever you have the opportunity to gain food from the birdfeeder" and the existing Great Crested Flycatcher ruling; this adds the explicit case of gaining a [die] and of ``if available'' powers, confirmed by the Wingspan Appendix quote in the thread.
64166.text: Gaining a [die] from the birdfeeder counts as gaining food, and a conditional power that would gain food (e.g. ``gain 1 [invertebrate] from the birdfeeder, if available'') also counts, so in both cases you may reroll the dice first if all [die] in the birdfeeder show the same face.
64166.title: Rerolling dice

64280.note: The thread also contains a separate official answer (comment 66113) that a bird whose food cost is [rodent]/[fish] counts as 1 icon, not 2, for the end-of-round goal counting [rodent] and [fish] in food costs. That is a distinct ruling about goal tiles and would need its own entry.
64280.text: \textbf{Willie-Wagtail}: you may reset the card tray only once per activation of this power. If no [card] with a [bowl] or [star] nest is available after that reset, you gain no card.

64431.note: Quoted from the Wingspan Asia appendix (page 6). Could arguably be general (``contiguous''), but only this card was discussed.
64431.text: For \textbf{Common Tailorbird}, ``contiguous'' means orthogonally adjacent: directly to the left, right, above, or below, never diagonal. The group may zig-zag across rows and columns as long as each bird in the group is orthogonally adjacent to at least one other bird in the group.

64451.note: Asia yellow (game end) power; the ruling rests on the scoring order shown on the reference tile.
64451.text: Eggs laid by \textbf{Common Tailorbird}'s end-of-game power do not count toward the round 4 end-of-round goal, because that goal is scored before game-end powers are activated. See the reference tile for the order of operations.

64503.note: The earlier part of the thread (comment 64508) restates the existing ruling that the bird only counts double for goals that count birds; the new content is the habitat count exceeding 5.
64503.text: When counting birds in a habitat for an end-of-round goal, \textbf{Greylag Goose} can push the total above 5: a bird that counts double may give you 6.

64580.note: The thread also mentions Common Grackle (``Common Crackle''), which was not supplied in the card list, so it is not attached. Consistent with the existing ``'May' creates a choice'' principle but adds that no alternative action may be substituted.
64580.text: ``May'' indicates a binary option: you may do exactly as instructed, or you may not do it at all. It never licenses substituting a different action. On \textbf{Blue Jay}, you may cache the gained [seed] on this bird or keep it in your personal supply, since you have already gained it. On \textbf{Pileated Woodpecker}, you may lay the additional [egg] on a [cavity] bird or lay no additional [egg] at all.
64580.title: May

64733.note: The answer also restates the published appendix entry for \textbf{Great Crested Grebe} and \textbf{Wilson's Storm Petrel} (cards drawn are kept separate and cannot be spent this turn); that part is a quote of existing rulebook text and could be added separately if desired.
64733.text: You do not need to keep a card in hand to satisfy \textbf{Wood Duck}'s power. If you draw 2 [card] with \textbf{Wood Duck} and then play or tuck all the cards in your hand (for example with \textbf{Common Chiffchaff}), having no card to discard at the end of your turn is legal.

64803.note: Answer confirms the questioner's premise; the copy happens but has no effect.
64803.text: A copied ``When Played'' power only does what it can do for the copying bird: \textbf{Rose-Ringed Parakeet} gains nothing by copying \textbf{Eastern Imperial Eagle}, because \textbf{Rose-Ringed Parakeet}'s cost contains no [rodent].

64865.note: Primarily a rule about the Asia duet map/goal mat rather than about \textbf{Small Minivet} itself; attached to the only card named. Second half of the thread is about a digital release and is not a ruling.
64865.text: A duet token placed in the reset box of the Asia goal mat cannot be removed to reset the bird tray or the birdfeeder on the same turn it was placed; only on a later turn. Duet tokens are placed between steps 5 and 6 of your turn, so a bird that lets you play an additional bird (e.g. \textbf{Small Minivet}) does not allow you to spend a token placed earlier in that same turn.

64895.text: You tuck 2 [card] from the deck behind \textbf{Galah} regardless of whether the other player you choose succeeds in gaining a [seed] from the birdfeeder.
