64906.note: The earlier official answer in this thread (comment 64907) states that tucked cards are essentially blank and only score 1 point each for the tucked-cards category; that is a separate general ruling and may already be covered by the existing corpus ("It's upside down, so none of the content on the tucked card matters").
64906.text: \textbf{Blue-Winged Warbler} may be played in either the [forest] or the [grassland].

65110.note: Jamey gave this answer in comment 65180, but in comment 109154 he acknowledged the Appendix wording is open to interpretation and said he would check with his team; no follow-up appears in the thread. Reviewer should verify whether a later official ruling supersedes this.
65110.reject_reason: hedged -- Jamey reopened it himself in comment 109154 -- see rejections.json
65110.text: Pink powers that trigger when another player's [predator] succeeds, such as \textbf{Turkey Vulture}, activate after that player has finished rolling for a push-your-luck hunt power (e.g. \textbf{Purple Heron}, \textbf{White-Throated Kingfisher}) and has gained at least something from it, not after each individual successful roll.

65118.reject_reason: Explains the red-cornered swift-start cards, a component/teaching-material question, not a rules clarification.

65151.note: Answer is a general Oceania rule about flightless birds; scoped here to the card named in the thread. Other flightless birds (e.g., Emu, Southern Brown Kiwi) share this rule but were not named.
65151.text: \textbf{Kākāpō} is flightless and has no printed wingspan; per page 3 of the Oceania rulebook, treat its wingspan as any length you want it to be (e.g., for end-of-round goals or bonus cards that reference wingspan).

65196.note: Scoped general because the definition of predator ``success'' governs all pink powers that trigger on another player's [predator] succeeding, but only Black Vulture is named in this thread.
65196.text: A [predator] power ``succeeds'' when its element of chance produces the result it is looking for (for example, looking at the top card of the deck and finding a bird with a small enough wingspan to tuck). \textbf{Black Vulture}'s power triggers whenever another player's [predator] finds what it is looking for.
65196.title: Predator success

65268.reject_reason: Clarifies a Swift Start guide walkthrough, not a rules question about cards or gameplay.

65835.reject_reason: Request/speculation about which birds are included in expansions; no rules content.

65930.note: Jamey confirmed only the turn-order premise and did not explicitly say the printed Verditer Flycatcher clarification is wrong; the ruling text infers that consequence. Reviewer may wish to soften or verify against a later official correction.
65930.reject_reason: wrong -- contradicts the printed Asia appendix on an inference -- see rejections.json
65930.text: On a turn, you first gain the core benefit of the row (food, eggs, or cards), then activate brown powers from right to left. Accordingly, the [invertebrate] referenced by the \textbf{Verditer Flycatcher} and the [egg] referenced by the \textbf{Grandala} must have been gained or laid before that bird is activated. (This corrects the Asia appendix clarification for the \textbf{Verditer Flycatcher}, which says the [invertebrate] may be gained before or after activating it.)

65975.note: Complements the existing rulings about copying/repeating: this one settles that the copied text is resolved from the copying bird's own perspective and habitat.
65975.text: Copy powers act as if the copied text were printed on the copying bird. So if \textbf{Superb Lyrebird} copies the \textbf{Northern Mockingbird}'s power, you then repeat a brown power on another bird in \textbf{Superb Lyrebird}'s own habitat ([forest]).

66019.text: When \textbf{Spotted Dove} moves to another player's mat, any cached food, [egg], or tucked [card] on it are discarded (Wingspan Asia appendix, p. 9).

66204.text: The two clauses of \textbf{Galah}'s power are independent; the order is simply order of operations. Even if the chosen player does not find a [seed] in the birdfeeder, you still tuck 2 [card] from the deck behind this bird.

66213.duplicates: Partially covered by the existing Tūī ruling: "Since being a predator power is a property of a power, this bird copying a predator power and the power succeeding counts as success of a predator power (e.g., for purposes of enabling the activation of a pink power on another player's mat, like that of the \textbf{Black Vulture})."
66213.note: Largely duplicates an existing Tūī ruling, but adds the general framing that the label transfers with the copied power, and would be new content on the Black-Billed Magpie page.
66213.text: When a power is copied, the entire power---including its label---transfers to the copying bird. So \textbf{Tūī} temporarily gains and activates a [predator] power when it copies one, which does trigger pink powers that respond to another player's [predator] succeeding, such as \textbf{Black-Billed Magpie}'s.

66335.text: \textbf{Great Indian Bustard}'s ``Also score it normally at game end'' only clarifies that scoring the bonus card immediately does not prevent scoring it again at game end; you score it at game end only if you still have that bonus card. If you later discard that same bonus card (for example with \textbf{Red-Crowned Crane}), you do not score it at game end.

66339.reject_reason: Complaint about real-world nest accuracy/errata list; no rules clarification given.

66507.reject_reason: Official answer was non-committal ("probably not, what is the exact text?") and never resolved.

66935.note: Bonus card; note that general rulings do not reach bonus cards in the current pipeline, but this is card-scoped so it should attach directly.
66935.text: Score only one habitat for the \textbf{Ecologist} bonus card. If two or three of your habitats are tied for the fewest birds, you still score just one of those habitats.

67298.note: Applies to the \textbf{Rainbow Enthusiast}-style color-name bonus cards; general rulings do not currently reach bonus card pages, so it is attached to \textbf{Silvereye}.
67298.text: For bonus cards that count birds with a color in their name, the color may be part of a larger word: \textbf{Silvereye} counts as a bird with a color in its name.
67298.title: Colors in bird names

67410.text: When a power resets the birdfeeder, such as \textbf{European Honey Buzzard}, all 5 dice are rerolled, including dice that players had already removed from the birdfeeder. This matches resetting the birdfeeder when all dice in it show the same face.

67926.duplicates: General ruling ``You may only reroll dice when gaining food from the birdfeeder and not when gaining food from the supply.'' covers the same principle, but this thread adds the rulebook-wording clarification and the two named cards.
67926.note: Closely related to the existing general reroll ruling (20190601); reviewer may prefer to attach only to the two Asia birds.
67926.reject_reason: Both Olive-Backed Sunbird and White-Browed Tit-Warbler already carry the general ruling
67926.text: You may only reset the birdfeeder when all dice in the birdfeeder show the same face and you are about to gain food \textit{from the birdfeeder}; the Asia rulebook's ``from the birdfeeder'' wording is a clarification of the original phrasing. Powers that let you roll a die and gain that food from the supply, such as \textbf{Olive-Backed Sunbird} and \textbf{White-Browed Tit-Warbler}, therefore do not give you an opportunity to reset the birdfeeder first.

67949.note: Jamey explicitly declined to answer, redirecting to Monster Couch.
67949.reject_reason: About a digital app achievement; not resolved and not a tabletop rules question

68210.duplicates: The only keywords that qualify a bird to count toward this bonus card are those listed thereon and those in the relevant sections of the expansion rulebooks.
68210.reject_reason: Already covered by the existing Anatomist keyword-list ruling; remainder is a house-rule allowance.

68350.note: The earlier official comment 68351 ("you can only spend food in your supply, not cached food") was corrected by Jamey in 124932 for these two birds; the retained ruling is the Winter Feeder clarification.
68350.text: [seed] cached on \textbf{Coal Tit} or \textbf{Eurasian Nuthatch} is not in your supply, so it does not count toward the \textbf{Winter Feeder} bonus card even though you may spend it at any time.

68394.text: If there is no [fish] on \textbf{Great Cormorant} when it is activated, ignore the first clause and skip straight to rolling 2 [die]; that clause only applies once there is a [fish] on this bird.

68704.text: If you have no birds in one of your habitats, your habitat with the fewest birds has 0 birds in it, so this bonus card scores 0 points.

69207.reject_reason: Fan design suggestions for future content; no rules question resolved.

69541.note: The thread also mentions woodswallows (e.g. Black-Faced Woodswallow, White-Breasted Woodswallow), but no such card was listed in the thread's card list, so only Wood Stork is attached.
69541.text: ``Wood'' (singular) in a bird's name is not a geography term for the \textbf{Cartographer} bonus card, so birds such as \textbf{Wood Stork} and woodswallows do not count.

69694.text: When this bird's power is activated, other players may choose not to lay an [egg].

70303.note: Two official comments; 127003 states the timing that settles it. Could also justify a general ruling on round-end power ordering vs. nectar discard, but scoped to the card discussed.
70303.text: The 2 [wild] gained with \textbf{Gray Wagtail}'s round-end power may be taken as [nectar], but round-end powers resolve before unused [nectar] is discarded, so that [nectar] is immediately lost.

70347.note: Second sentence about an empty birdfeeder follows from the card's ``if there is one'' wording; the official answer addressed only the removal of the die.
70347.text: The food cached by \textbf{Willow Tit} comes from the birdfeeder, so the corresponding die must be removed from the birdfeeder. If the birdfeeder contains no [invertebrate], [seed], or [fruit], nothing is cached.

71876.note: Complements the existing general ruling ``Regular reroll rules apply whenever you have the opportunity to gain food from the birdfeeder.'' Two official comments contribute (71887 and 90024); 71887 is the one that settles the core reroll rule. No specific cards were named that the rule attaches to, so a predicate is needed.
71876.text: Unless a card specifically says otherwise, the birdfeeder dice may be rerolled in exactly two situations: when the birdfeeder is empty of dice, immediately refill it by rolling all 5 dice; and when a player is about to gain food and all dice in the birdfeeder show the exact same face, that player may choose to refill the birdfeeder by rolling all 5 dice. There is no default option to pay food to reset the birdfeeder, and a bonus on the Oceania player mat that allows a reset may be used only once per turn.
71876.title: Rerolling dice

71894.note: Stated as a general definition of "neighbor"; other cards use the same term, but only Eurasian Hoopoe was named in the thread.
71894.text: Your neighbors are only the players directly to your right and left — at most 2 players, regardless of the number of players in the game.

72045.text: Playing \textbf{Red Kite} on top of another bird in a player's [grassland] still counts as playing a bird in that habitat, so it triggers \textbf{Horned Lark}.

75435.note: Existing Common Swift ruling notes that unused [nectar] can be spent as blue powers are activated — that refers to spending it where a power allows [wild]/any food; this ruling clarifies it cannot substitute for the specific [invertebrate] requirement. A reviewer may want to reconcile the two.
75435.text: [nectar] cannot be used to pay the [invertebrate] discard for this bird's power. When a bird power refers to a specific food type, [nectar] is not a wild food.

81381.duplicates: If you use this bird's power to play another bird with a ``play a second bird'' power, you may then use the latter bird's power to play yet another bird.
81381.note: Largely duplicates the existing chaining ruling on all three cards; the only new content is the reminder to pay both the food cost and the column [egg] cost for each bird played.
81381.text: You may chain ``play an additional bird'' powers together, playing several birds in a single turn, as long as you pay each bird's printed food cost and the [egg] cost at the top of the column it is placed in.

85505.text: With \textbf{Forster's Tern} you are not required to keep a card in hand for the end-of-turn discard; if you have tucked or otherwise used all of your cards, there is nothing to discard. \textbf{Great Crested Grebe} and \textbf{Wilson's Storm Petrel} work differently: keep the cards drawn with those powers separate from your hand until the end of your turn, when you keep 1 of them and discard the rest.

86745.note: The thread's second question (moving two birds to another habitat in the same turn, comment 105058) is separate and is already covered by the existing rulings stating that the action cube does not change habitats with the bird; only the Anatomist answer is proposed here. Note tension with the existing Anatomist ruling that substrings not referring to body parts do not count (e.g. the \textit{wing} in \textbf{Burrowing Owl}) -- Jamey nevertheless allows \textbf{Desert Wheatear}.
86745.text: \textbf{Desert Wheatear} counts toward the \textbf{Anatomist} bonus card (``ear'').

98212.text: \textbf{Red Junglefowl} counts toward the \textbf{Cartographer} bonus card, since ``jungle'' appears in its name.
